title: God's Provision
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
What if everything you needed to live well was already available to you, and you just didn't know how to access it? And what if the reason so many people feel like they're falling short has nothing to do with what they lack?

In this sermon, Ps Keith Ainge unpacks a single verse from 2 Peter that carries more weight than most people realise. He works through six ideas packed into just 27 words, and the way he connects ancient scripture to everyday life, from flat-pack furniture to a Ford Prefect in the backyard, makes it genuinely hard to look away. There's something here about the difference between knowing about someone and actually knowing them, and why that distinction might be the most important thing you explore this year.

Sit down and give this one a watch.

title: The Guarantee
speaker: Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the Christian life you've been living is actually just the starting line, not the finish line? And what if there's a genuine guarantee attached to how you build from here?

In this sermon, Andrew Cartledge opens up a series through one of the most overlooked corners of the New Testament, and the question he keeps coming back to is both simple and uncomfortable: are you burying what you've been given, or actually doing something with it? He draws on some unexpected stories, a cringe-worthy high school athletics moment, a workplace analogy, and a parable that most people think they already know, to frame something that might reframe how you think about faith entirely. If you've ever felt like your spiritual life is running but going nowhere, this is worth your time.

Watch now and find out what the guarantee actually says.

title: Authority to Grow
speaker: Ron Spence
blurb:
"Be strong and courageous" sounds like a call to try harder. But what if authority doesn't come from effort at all?

Pastor Ron Spence takes an unexpected path through Robin Williams, Elmer Fudd, and a centurion who understood something that most people never figure out. He unpacks why so many people stay stuck, why imagination can be more dangerous than circumstance, and what it actually looks like to carry the kind of authority that changes things. This one moves around a lot, but it keeps landing in the same place, and by the end you'll see exactly why that place matters.

If you've ever felt like you were working harder than the results showed, sit with this one for a while. It might answer a question you didn't know you were carrying.

title: Harvest Church Sunday Service 10:30AM
blurb:
What if the biggest barrier to doing something meaningful isn't your lack of resources, your lack of confidence, or even your lack of calling, but simply the way you've been thinking about your role? And what if a story you've heard a hundred times actually contains something you've completely missed?

In this episode, Pastor Joel brings a fresh set of eyes to one of the most familiar miracles in the Bible, and the result is genuinely uncomfortable in the best way. He traces a shift in how Jesus related to the people around him, a shift that reframes what it means to belong to a church community. Along the way he shares stories from his own life that are honest, funny, and surprisingly convicting. By the end, you'll find yourself asking a question you might not have considered before.

Hit play and find out what Jesus actually said when the people around him pointed out a problem they expected someone else to fix.

title: The Time is NOW for Surrender
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
1 - God starts with what you already have.

2 - God works through what feels insignificant

3 - God multiplies what is freely given

Three Practical applications

- Identify your rod, what do you have?

- Surrender it to God, be a steward for the Kingdom

We've got enough love for this!

- Use what is in your hand boldly, do not be hesitant, step out with faith

title: The Time is NOW to Expand
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of faith that looks a lot like financial caution. It waits for the right conditions, protects what it has, and calls that wisdom. Ps Andrew Cartledge isn't so sure that version is actually faith at all.

In this episode, he does something you don't often hear from a pastor. He steps up to the microphone and starts with an apology. What follows is an honest, unfiltered conversation about generosity, vision, and what it actually looks like when a church decides to stop playing it safe. There's a story from scripture that makes absolutely no economic sense, a farming analogy that reframes everything you thought you knew about what you have in your hand, and a vision for 2026 that is, by the pastor's own admission, a massive call to something bigger than comfort.

If you've ever wondered whether a local church can genuinely change the world, this one is worth your time. Settle in and let this one land.

title: The Time is NOW for Breakthrough
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb: Ps Keith unpacks week 2 of our Vision Month. You will be blessed and challenged to let rivers of living water flow through you.

title: Altars or Thrones?
speaker: Greg McKinnon
blurb:
You scroll past your phone for the third time in ten minutes, or you catch yourself replaying a conversation you lost two days ago, or you notice that a certain number in your bank account is the only thing standing between you and feeling okay. None of that looks like idolatry. But it might be.

In this episode, Greg McKinnon takes an ancient showdown between a prophet and 450 false prophets and holds it up like a mirror to modern life. The question Elijah put to a divided nation turns out to be surprisingly personal, and surprisingly uncomfortable. Greg works through why the human heart has a way of building loyalty to things that promise everything and deliver something very different, and what it actually looks like to notice when that is happening in your own life.

This one will probably ask you to sit with something you would rather keep scrolling past.

title: Don't Open the Door
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
There is a detail in this sermon that keeps coming back: a door. Not a dramatic entrance, not a grand metaphor, just a door, and what Ps Rachel Cartledge notices about it is the thing most of us have been quietly hoping nobody would point out.

She takes one of the oldest stories in the Bible and makes it feel uncomfortably close to home. She is not here to lecture or condemn, but she is honest enough to name what most of us would rather leave unnamed: the patterns, habits, and emotions that crouch quietly in our lives, waiting for a moment of weakness. What she shares is both a warning and a genuine source of hope, and the way she gets there might surprise you.

Settle in and let this one land.

title: Everyday Heroes - Jonah
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
If you have ever felt a flash of resentment when grace landed somewhere you thought it had no business going, Jonah might be the prophet you never expected to find yourself in.

Jonah is one of the strangest figures in the Bible, and in this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge makes a case that he might also be the most relatable. This is not the tidy children's story that ends with a fish and a lesson about obedience. There is a fourth chapter that most people skip, and it is the part that will sit with you longest. Andrew walks through the full arc of Jonah's story, including the anger, the popcorn, the plant, and the question that hangs in the air with no resolution, and asks what it reveals about the way we actually follow God when our hearts resist what grace is doing.

Settle in and let this one land.

title: Everyday Heroes - Joseph
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Some people's lives seem to fall apart in slow motion, one setback at a time, until the original dream feels almost embarrassing to remember. Joseph knew exactly what that was like. He had a God-given dream, and then watched his life unravel, not once, not twice, but again and again.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a fresh look at one of the Bible's most well-known stories and finds something in it that might surprise you. This is not the Sunday school version. Joseph's journey from the pit to the prison to the palace is a story about what it means to stay faithful when nobody is watching, when the dream feels impossible, and when the path forward makes no sense. There is something here for anyone who has ever felt overlooked, set up, or completely out of their depth.

By the end, you will understand what Ps Andrew means when he says the palace was never really the point.

title: Everyday Hero's
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Your flaws are not the problem. They never were.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a look at some of the most celebrated figures in the Bible and asks why we keep putting them on pedestals when they clearly did not deserve to be there. From fear to impatience to outright deception, these heroes had real cracks in them, and yet somehow that did not disqualify them from being used in remarkable ways. What Andrew uncovers in the story of Abraham might just reframe the way you think about your own doubts, your own failures, and what faith actually looks like when it gets tested in real time.

Maybe the thing standing between you and everything God has promised is not your circumstances at all. Maybe it is you. And maybe that is worth sitting with for a while.

title: Everyday Heroes - Noah
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
God saw that the wickedness of man was great, and yet somehow, in the middle of all of it, one ordinary person kept showing up and doing the next right thing.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge kicks off a brand new series called Everyday Heroes by taking a long look at one of the most familiar Bible stories around. But don't let the familiarity fool you. This is not the children's Sunday school version. Andrew unpacks what it actually cost Noah to say yes to something he had never seen before, couldn't fully explain, and wouldn't live to fully understand. Along the way, he asks some uncomfortable questions about why we keep waiting for certainty before we take a single step forward.

By the end, Andrew lands on a phrase that is so simple it almost sounds like a letdown, until you sit with it long enough to realise it might be the most honest thing anyone has said to you about faith in a long time.

title: Arise Shine
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
Primary Points

1 - The world was in darkness

2 - Light overcomes the darkness

3 - The Light bring radiance and Joy

title: Communion Service
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge, Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume the broken parts of their story are the parts God has to work around. The failures, the shame, the sense of having gone too far. But that assumption misses something hiding in plain sight across the whole of Scripture.

In this episode, Ps Andrew and Ps Rachel Cartledge take three ancient stories that most people know only on the surface and reveal a pattern stitched through the Bible from its earliest pages. Once you see it, you cannot unsee it. This service builds slowly and deliberately toward a moment around the communion table that reframes what it means to belong, to be forgiven, and to be connected to the people sitting right beside you. There is a thread running through history, and it leads directly to you. By the end, you will look around the room differently.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: Youth Take Over
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
Some people assume handing the service over to the youth just means a fun, low-key Sunday where the usual stuff gets swapped out for something a little more casual. This week, that assumption gets tested.

Our Empire Youth team are taking over the Sunday Service completely, and what they bring to it might just surprise you.

It won't cost you nothing to tune in, but it might cost you the idea that youth ministry is just a warm-up act.

title: Harvest Church Sunday Service 10:30AM
blurb:
Most people are waiting for proof before they prepare, and that is exactly what keeps them stuck.

This sermon from Harvest Church digs into a tension that most of us feel but rarely name: the gap between where we are and where we sense we could be. Drawing on stories from Scripture that range from a widow with almost nothing to a man building a boat before rain existed, this episode unpacks three surprisingly practical moves that anyone can make right now, before anything miraculous shows up. There is something here that will challenge the way you think about readiness, generosity, and what it actually means to trust something bigger than yourself.

If you have ever felt like you are holding back until conditions are right, this one is for you.

title: Faith that Fails
speaker: Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine you genuinely believe something, you could articulate it clearly if someone asked, and yet somehow you keep living like it isn't true. Not because you stopped caring. Not because you've given up. Just because there's a gap there that doesn't seem to close no matter what you do.

Andrew Cartledge gets honest about that disconnect in this episode, the one most people feel but rarely say out loud: knowing what you're supposed to believe and actually living it out are two very different things. He works through three specific reasons why faith stalls, and at least one of them will probably feel uncomfortably familiar. This isn't a pep talk and it isn't a guilt trip. It's an honest look at what gets in the way, and why the answer might be simpler and more confronting than you'd expect.

Maybe the more interesting question isn't whether your faith is failing, but which part of it is, and whether you've ever actually stopped to look.

title: Impossible Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
What if the thing standing between you and everything God has for you isn't doubt, but the order you've got things in? What if you've been waiting for proof before you're willing to move, and that's exactly the problem?

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest and sometimes uncomfortable look at a tension most people feel but rarely admit: knowing God can do something extraordinary, while quietly suspecting he probably won't. Drawing from a passage in Isaiah that most people read in isolation, he unpacks what gets missed when you pull it away from its context, and what it reveals about the way growth, faith, and action are actually meant to work together. There's a moment in here where the gap between believing and trusting becomes impossible to ignore, and it might just reframe the way you think about what you've been waiting for.

Press play and see where this one takes you.

title: Thirsty
speaker: Greg McKinnon
blurb: Jesus said I have water that if you drink you will never thirst again. But how do we access it? Join us as Ps Greg unpack this powerful encounter at the well.

title: The Lord's Prayer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: When we pray and fast we create an intimacy with God that cannot be found any other way.

title: Impossible Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: A man stands at the edge of the unknown, choosing to trust a God he cannot see, convinced that somehow, stepping forward is the only real option. That's the heartbeat of Hebrews 11:6, and it's exactly where Pastor Andrew Cartledge takes us in this episode, unpacking what it actually looks like to live out an impossible faith. Give it a listen and see where it takes you.

title: How's your throw
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Ps Rachel unpacks this beautiful passage in 1 Peter 5:7 and looks at all the ways we refuse to let the Lord help us when things get tough.

title: Keys to an anointed life
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself settling, not because you had to, but because stopping felt reasonable enough and the people around you seemed to agree?

In this episode, Ps Keith Ainge walks through one of the most gripping stories in the Old Testament and finds something in it that feels startlingly relevant to everyday life. There is a journey involved, with real stopping points that look like perfectly good reasons to quit, and the tension between where you are and where you are supposed to be is something most people will recognise immediately. Keith brings in moments from his own life that are honest and a little surprising, and by the time the episode reaches its destination, the question it leaves you with is a quiet but persistent one.

You won't hear the word "enough" the same way again.

title: Stuck in the Desert
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Pastor Andrew explains how fear controls our life and blows things out of proportion. If we are to step into the promised land, we must wage ware on fear!

title: Harvest Kids Animated Bible Story
blurb: Our incredible Harvest Kids join Pastor Andrew for a retelling of the 12 Spies who scouted the promised land.

title: Who Me?
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb: Ps Caleb unpacks the identity crisis that Saul went throguh as he was announced king.

title: What I See
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Ps Andrew starts to outline vision and direction for our future as a church. We have looked at Mission: What we do. We have looked at Values: Who we are. Now it's time for Vision: Where we are going.

The important question to ask ourselves is can you see what we see?

title: Pass It On
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
If you've ever felt like the most important things you leave behind have nothing to do with your actual achievements, this one is worth your time.

Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church gets into what it really looks like to hand something worth keeping to the people coming after us. This is not a neat list of tips for parents. It goes into the messy, honest territory of how we handle money, how we treat the people around us, and the gap between the relationships we talk about and the ones we actually model. There are moments here that will make you laugh, and moments that might make you a little uncomfortable, in the best possible way.

Worth the listen.

title: 6. The Final Word
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: The finale of our Revelation Series! Ps Andrew brings it all home with a perspective on the already won battle and the victorious King of all Kings.

title: Change Your Mind
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
...because here's the thing: it's already here. You just might not be seeing it yet.

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson unpacks one of the most repeated ideas in the entire Bible, yet one of the most misunderstood in everyday life. She traces a thread from John the Baptist through to Jesus, from ancient parables to a connect group meeting in a country town, and somewhere in the middle she challenges the way most of us have been thinking about God's rule, God's presence, and what we actually have access to right now. This isn't a history lesson. It's an invitation to reconsider something that might be closer than you think.

The phrase Ps Ruth keeps coming back to is "at hand," and by the end of this episode, you'll never hear those two words the same way again.

title: Who do you say that I Am?
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Join Ps Rachel Cartledge as she explores one of Jesus' most profound questions: 'Who do you say that I am?' Discover how this question isn't just for the disciples, but for each of us today. Be challenged, encouraged, and inspired to reflect on your personal understanding of Jesus and what it truly means to follow Him.

title: 5. The Counterfeit Kingdom
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Who is this motley crew we see represented in Revelation 12-13? The dragon, two beasts and the harlot. What is the mark of the beast? Join us as we explore the true mark and unmask the counterfeit kingdom.

title: 4. Divine Judgement
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Seals, Trumpets and Bowls. How do we make sense of it all? It's simple if you keep your eyes on Jesus.

title: What are we doing with what we've been given?
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
Most people assume that if they just had a little more, they'd do a little more. More time, more money, more opportunity. But that assumption might be exactly what's getting in the way.

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin walks through one of Jesus' most confronting parables and asks a question that is simple on the surface but surprisingly difficult to sit with. You'll hear why comparison might be more spiritually dangerous than you've realised, what faithfulness actually looks like when the spotlight isn't on you, and why the gap between what you've been given and what you do with it matters more than you might think. This is the kind of conversation that has a way of sneaking up on you.

Wherever you're at right now, this is probably the right moment to hear it.

title: The Lord, my Shepherd
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
The oldest poem in the world already has the answer you've been looking for.

In this episode, Ps Keith Ainge takes one of the most familiar passages in the entire Bible and finds a way to make it feel completely new. He draws on shepherds, sheep, dark valleys, and a life lived through real hardship to ask what it actually means to be known, guided, and cared for by someone who has already been where you are. This is not a comfortable, tidy sermon. It is honest about the hard parts of life and surprisingly tender about what meets you there. You might be surprised by how much of it lands.

You'll come away with a quieter, clearer sense of what it means to not be alone in the places you thought no one else knew about.

title: LOOPHOLES
blurb:
There's a version of faith that looks a lot like knowing all the right answers and using them to avoid actually changing anything. Ron knows that version well, and in this episode he's honest about it.

From orphanages and boarding schools to fake identities, tax schemes, and a very questionable driver's licence, Ron traces the journey of someone who understood the rules, the beliefs, the promises, and still found every possible reason not to live by them. Drawing on the parable of the prodigal son, this sermon asks a question that cuts deeper than most: what is the difference between knowing about a father and actually coming home to one? The answer might surprise you, and it might land closer to home than you're expecting.

This one is worth sitting with someone after you've listened.

title: 3. The Throne Room of Heaven
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume heaven is a quiet, hazy place, somewhere peaceful and vaguely distant. Revelation chapters four and five suggest something else entirely.

In this episode, Pastor Andrew Cartledge opens up one of the most vivid and strange scenes in all of scripture, the throne room vision where ancient creatures covered in eyes circle a throne, crowns are hurled at someone's feet, and a moment of devastating silence breaks open into something almost impossible to describe. Along the way, Andrew unpacks why a lion becomes a lamb, what thunder and lightning are doing in heaven, and why what you do on a Sunday morning might be more connected to eternity than you ever realised.

Closer than you think.

title: 2. Letters from Jesus
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You can do everything right, work hard, stay doctrinally sound, serve faithfully, and still be missing the one thing that matters most.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up two of the most personal chapters in the book of Revelation, the letters Jesus dictated to real churches facing real pressure. What emerges is not a theological puzzle to solve but something far more confronting and far more tender. You will hear about a church that had everything going for it, and the single sentence from Jesus that stopped it cold. There is also something in the structure of these letters that, once you see it, you cannot unsee it, and it reframes the whole book entirely.

This one's for anyone who needs to hear it.

title: 1. The Revelation of Jesus
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Revelation is not a code to crack but a Christ to behold. It was written to comfort, not confuse; 

to unveil Christ, not conceal truth

In this message, we tackle the most misunderstood book in the Bible. Discover why Revelation isn't about fear or end-times speculation, but about unveiling Jesus Christ Himself.

Learn 7 essential principles for properly reading Revelation, understand the first-century context that changes everything, and witness John's magnificent vision of the glorified Christ. This foundational message reveals why Revelation has been a source of hope for believers for 2,000 years.

Perfect for anyone wanting to understand Revelation through Scripture rather than popular fiction. Come see Jesus as "the Alpha and the Omega" - faithful in the past, sovereign in the present, and triumphant in the future.

title: Abiding in Christ
speaker: Greg McKinnon
blurb:
If you have ever felt like staying committed to something costs more than just walking away, you are probably closer to what Jesus was describing than you think.

In this sermon, Greg McKinnon works through one of the most vivid images Jesus ever used to describe what it looks like to follow him. There is a lot here that might surprise you, including an honest look at what the earliest followers of Jesus actually experienced, a question about whether comfort might be quietly pulling you off course, and a fresh way of thinking about pain, pruning, and what it means to actually stay. Greg brings warmth and humour to some genuinely confronting ideas, and the result is something that feels less like a lecture and more like a conversation you did not know you needed.

You will finish this one with a different way of thinking about difficulty, and a clearer sense of what it actually means to stay close to something worth staying close to.

title: Pentecost Sunday
speaker: Ps Daniel Bates
blurb:
What if the moment that changes everything arrives not with a whisper, but like a bolt of lightning you never saw coming? And what if most people miss it simply because they stopped expecting it?

In this episode, Ps Daniel Bates takes the stage on Pentecost Sunday at Harvest Church and brings something you might not expect from a church sermon: raw honesty about why so many people talk about the Holy Spirit but never actually experience anything. He traces a thread from a century-old revival on the east coast of Australia, through a family legacy that reads like something stranger than fiction, all the way to a street in Los Angeles where grown adults stood at a gate and wept without knowing why. Along the way he asks a question that might quietly unsettle you: what happens when you stop being a witness who performs and start being a person who actually receives? There is warmth here, and humour, and a few moments that are genuinely hard to explain away.

Hit play and find out what happened to the six year old who got carried home stiff as a board from a church service in Adelaide.

title: I live with an Honouring Heart
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself in a moment where you had the upper hand, and felt the pull to use it?

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a question that sounds simple on the surface and unpacks why most of us get it completely backwards. Through a cave, a robe, a pair of scissors, and an Olympic sprint that changed everything, you will start to see honour not as a nicety or a church custom but as something with real weight and real consequences. There is a story in here that will reframe how you think about the moments when you have the upper hand, and what you choose to do with it.

This one has a way of staying with you, and you might find yourself wanting to talk it through with someone once you have heard it.

title: I LIVE by the Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there's the version of faith that sounds good on paper. On the other, there's the daily reality of pushing harder, trying to be better, and wondering why it never quite works.

In this sermon from Galatians 5, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a surprisingly honest look at what it actually means to live by the Spirit, not just believe in it. He gets into the stuff nobody likes to talk about, including a very long list in the Bible that might hit closer to home than you'd expect. Along the way there's a story about Roger Bannister, a jar of ping pong balls, and a question that reframes everything: it's not whether you have the Spirit, it's whether the Spirit has you.

If you've ever felt like you're running the race alone, this one's for you.

title: I Live on the Bright Side
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself smiling and saying you're fine, even when you really aren't? Most of us have been there, pushing through hard seasons and hoping the feeling of joy will eventually show up if we just hold it together long enough.

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson takes a look at what joy really is, and just as importantly, what it isn't. She cuts through the noise around happiness, positive thinking, and spiritual performance to get to something that feels surprisingly honest and grounded. You'll hear why the people who seem to carry the most joy are rarely the ones with the easiest lives, and what that tells us about where this kind of joy actually comes from.

This one's for anyone who's starting to wonder if there's something more solid underneath all the striving.

title: I Live and Learn
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
The harder you try to grow, the more your blind spots tend to stay exactly where they are. That tension is at the centre of this episode, and it turns out the reason most of us stay stuck isn't our circumstances, our past, or even our struggles. It's the posture of our heart.

Ps Caleb McLaughlin takes a look at what it really means to stay teachable, and why so many of us end up repeating the same patterns, the same arguments, and the same frustrations year after year without ever quite figuring out why. Through a surprisingly relatable story from a mechanic shop, some honest reflections on pride, and a closer look at what scripture actually says about humility and growth, this episode will have you asking some questions about yourself that you might have been avoiding. It's the kind of conversation that doesn't let you off the hook easily, but somehow still feels like an invitation rather than a lecture.

Are you actually open to growing, or just telling yourself you are?

Teachable.

title: I Live a life of Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people think faith is about believing hard enough, and that if you just hold on to the right convictions, that counts. But there is a gap between what we say we believe and how we actually live, and it is more revealing than most of us are comfortable admitting.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at what faith actually is, and it might not be what you think. He works through some of the most common ways people misunderstand faith, including the versions that sound spiritual but quietly let us off the hook. There is a moment in this sermon where the distinction between faith and faithfulness lands in a way that is hard to shake, and it raises a question worth sitting with long after you finish listening.

This one is for anyone who has ever wondered why believing something and actually living by it can feel like two very different things.

title: Resurrection Sunday
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people treat Easter as a calendar event, something to acknowledge and then move on from. But Ps Andrew Cartledge thinks that framing misses the point entirely, and in this Easter Sunday sermon from Harvest Church, he makes a quiet but convincing case for why.

Drawing from 1 Peter, he opens up what it actually means to live with expectation. Not as a vague religious sentiment, not as wishful thinking, but as something anchored in a real historical moment. He walks through the difference between approaching life from a "before Friday" perspective and an "after Sunday" one, and why that single shift changes the way you face whatever is in front of you right now. This is the kind of sermon that meets you where you are, whatever you walked in carrying.

If Easter really is the most important event in human history, maybe it was never meant to stay on the calendar.

title: Good Friday Service
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us have never quite known what to do with Good Friday. It asks something of us that is hard to name, a weight that sits just beneath the surface of the story, and it is easy to move through it quickly just to get to Sunday.

In this Good Friday service from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge traces the final hours of Jesus with a focus that might surprise you. From the last supper to the garden to the trial, there is a thread running through this story that reframes everything you thought you knew about why Good Friday is called good. The sermon sits with the weight of what actually happened, not to leave you there, but to remind you that Friday only makes sense when you know what Sunday holds.

You won't hear the cross the same way again.

title: The Road to Grief
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Jesus wept when He saw Jerusalem. He wept because they will reject Him and miss the day of their visitation. Pastor Andrew leads us on a journey following Jesus from Galilee to Gethsemane to Golgotha to the Grave and on to Glory. This Easter is all about Jesus!

title: I Live for Others
speaker: Alison Creek
blurb:
Paul is sitting in a prison cell, writing a letter he knows will outlive him. He isn't focused on his own circumstances. He's thinking about the people who will read his words, the ones he loves and hasn't stopped praying for, the ones he's given his life to serve.

That posture, of living genuinely oriented toward others, is what Alison Creek unpacks in this sermon. She gets honest about what it actually looks like day to day, not as an inspiring concept but as something you'd have to choose over and over again. She brings an in-the-room illustration that will quietly reframe where you see yourself in the picture, and she walks through three areas of life that most of us would rather skip past. There's something here whether you feel stretched thin from giving or you're not sure you have much to offer. Alison speaks with warmth and no pretension, and this one has a way of settling in slowly and staying there.

Three volunteers show up in this sermon. One of them is probably you. Follow that thread and see where it takes you.

title: I Live Through the Word
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Not as solid as you think.

Ps Andrew Cartledge opens with a jaw-dropping real-life story from the Mornington Peninsula, and it sets up something worth sitting with: what does it actually mean to build your life on something that holds? This is not a lecture about reading your Bible more. It is an honest look at why so many people find themselves standing in the rubble of things they thought were secure, and what the difference is between people who make it through the hard seasons and people who don't. You might be surprised how practical and direct this gets.

This is probably one to listen to with someone else nearby, because you will want to talk about it after.

title: I Live Generously
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
And the frustrating thing is, you already know this on some level. Holding on tighter has never actually made you feel more secure. Chasing more has never quite delivered the satisfaction you were hoping for. Yet every instinct you have keeps pulling you in that direction anyway.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge explores one of the most counterintuitive ideas in human history, that giving freely actually makes you better off than holding on. She brings in some surprising science, a story about a Samaritan that is stranger than you might remember, and a refreshingly honest look at why generosity is so hard even for people who genuinely want to be good. This is not a lecture about money. It is a conversation about time, about sacrifice, about what it actually costs to be the kind of person who shows up for others, and whether you are willing to go there.

Find out what Ps Rachel means when she asks whether you are willing to cross the road.

title: Strong & Courageous
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of faith that looks a lot like standing still. You know what you've been promised, you can almost see it from where you are, but everything in front of you feels too big, too uncertain, too much. And so you wait. Most of us have been there more times than we'd like to admit.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the oldest leadership moments in the Bible and finds something that feels surprisingly current. He traces the story of twelve ordinary people sent to scout out a promised land, and asks why only two of them are remembered. From there, he unpacks a three-word command repeated three times in four verses, explores what it actually means in the original Hebrew, and lands on four conditions that separate people who inherit a promise from people who just talk about it. There is something here about individual courage, something about what happens when a community decides to move together, and something about the kind of obedience that most of us quietly avoid.

You won't hear courage the same way again.

title: Keys to Breakthough
speaker: Ps Phil Shand
blurb:
A man stands outside a closed door and knocks. He keeps knocking. The promise Jesus gives in Matthew 7 sounds simple enough, almost too simple, but most people have heard it so many times it barely registers anymore.

In this episode, Ps Phil Shand brings a surprisingly practical and honest look at what breakthrough actually requires. He draws on that familiar promise and unpacks it in a way that might catch you off guard. There are three specific keys he works through, and each one challenges a quiet assumption you might not even know you're carrying. Whether you're facing something in your health, your relationships, your finances, or just a low season you can't seem to climb out of, this episode has something worth sitting with.

Maybe the question isn't whether the door opens. Maybe it's whether you've been standing in the right place all along.

title: Reaching the World
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this powerful message, we explore the transformative journey of loving God, growing together, and reaching the world. The central theme is love—loving God with all our heart, soul, and mind, and extending that love to our neighbors and the world. Join us as we delve into the profound concept of agape love, not just as a theological term, but as a practical guide for our lives. Discover how discipleship and evangelism are key to living out this calling, and how we can impact the world by living selflessly, putting others before ourselves. Whether you're new to faith or have been walking with Christ for years, this message will inspire you to deepen your understanding and practice of love in your everyday life.

title: Growing Together
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Faith isn't meant to be a solo journey—we grow stronger together. Matthew 22 calls us to love God and love others, and Acts 2:42 shows us a church devoted to teaching, fellowship, and prayer. Real growth happens in genuine relationships, where we sharpen one another like iron. Are we willing to invest, be vulnerable, and serve sacrificially? Let's build a community that reflects Christ's love!

title: Loving God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this inspiring sermon, Pastor Andrew launches a new series at Harvest Church, emphasising the core mission of the church: "Loving God, Growing Together, Reaching the World." He breaks down the importance of embracing these principles as a unified community, stressing that a mission only has power when fully understood and lived out by everyone. Through a deep dive into loving God with all our heart, soul, and mind, Pastor Andrew challenges the congregation to commit to a transformational Christian lifestyle. Join us as we explore how these simple yet profound concepts can lead to personal growth and a stronger communal bond.

title: Change Of Heart - 9th February 2025
speaker: Ron Spence
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself wondering how someone you respect, someone with years of good living behind them, could fall apart so completely and so fast?

In this sermon, Ron Spence draws on one of the darkest stories in the entire Bible to explore a distinction most people have never stopped to consider: the difference between changing your mind and having a change of heart. He connects an ancient royal tragedy to the quiet epidemic happening in churches, communities, and families right now, and the picture he paints is both unsettling and strangely hopeful. Along the way, he shares some surprisingly candid moments from his own life and the lives of people he loves, and the honesty of it lands harder than any polished argument could.

This is the kind of episode worth coming back to, because the thing it's asking you to guard is easy to forget and costly to lose.

title: An Everyday Faith
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
Most people assume that feeling stuck or exhausted in their spiritual life means they're not trying hard enough. More discipline, more effort, more willpower. That's the usual answer. But what if the pressure itself is the problem, and the whole framework is off?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin from Harvest Church takes an honest look at why so many of us feel the gap between who we want to be and where we actually are. He explores what it really looks like to follow Jesus not as a goal to achieve or a box to tick, but as something lived out one ordinary day at a time. Along the way, he unpacks a familiar prayer that most people have heard but few have sat with long enough to notice what it's actually saying about daily surrender, daily struggle, and daily provision.

This one has a way of staying with you. Worth listening to with someone you can talk it through with after.

title: Return, Rebuild, Renew - The Book of Ezra
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
If you've ever felt like you were starting over from scratch, with less than you had before and no real reason to expect it to work out, the book of Ezra might be the last place you'd think to look for company. But it turns out to be a surprisingly good place to find it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up a corner of the Bible most people have never visited, and finds a story that is far stranger and more compelling than anyone expects. A captive nation, a pagan king with an unlikely nudge from God, and a rebuilding project that nobody should have been able to afford, let alone get funded by the very empire that took everything in the first place. But woven through the history and the genealogies is something that reaches right into the present: questions about resistance, resolve, identity, and what it actually looks like to return to something you thought was gone for good. This one moves between ancient Babylon and everyday life faster than you'd think possible.

The book of Ezra has something to say about the life you are trying to rebuild right now. Give it a listen.

title: Beauty for Ashes
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Sometimes life takes a turn you didn't see coming, and suddenly the version of yourself you thought you knew is standing in the middle of something you don't have a map for. The plans are gone, the familiar is gone, and you're left wondering how you got here and where here even is.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge shares something she almost didn't preach. Starting with an honest look at a year marked by loss, grief, and unexpected change, she traces a thread from ancient ruins to a simple drive past scorched bushland, and finds a promise tucked inside one of the oldest books of the Bible. What unfolds is a surprisingly tender exploration of what it looks like when hope shows up in the last place you'd think to look for it, and what it might cost you to hold onto the rubble instead.

Give this one a listen, and let it sit with you.

title: Rediscovering the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Ps Andrew takes us on a discovery of the Holy Spirit. Who He is, What He does and how we are baptised.

title: Life and Light
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
In this sermon we explore some big concepts about who Jesus is through the book of John 1:1-5

You will be blessed to know He is your life and light!

title: Christmas Eve at Harvest Church
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Join us for a beautiful evening of carols, worship, fun and games as well as a powerful Gospel message about Christ the King.

title: Don't Drink the Poison
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
And yeah, it might be the very thing you've been carrying the longest.

Ps Andrew Cartledge gets into something most of us would rather avoid, especially around Christmas. He starts with a question the whole room has to answer honestly, and from there he unpacks why so many people, including church people, find themselves quietly stuck, carrying an old wound from years ago like it happened yesterday. There's a moment in this sermon where a single paragraph gets read aloud and the room goes silent, because everyone recognises themselves in it. That moment alone is worth your time.

If you're heading into the holidays with any unresolved weight sitting on your chest, this one is exactly the right thing to listen to right now.

title: Come to the Table
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge, Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: Join us for a powerful sermon exploring the profound significance of the table in Scripture as a place of reconciliation and unity. Discover how the early church, amidst a backdrop of division and tension, demonstrated radical equality at the table through the unifying power of the Gospel. This message delves into stories of biblical reconciliation, such as Joseph and his brothers, David and Mephibosheth, and Jesus' interactions during the Last Supper. Be inspired by the table's symbolism as a place of grace, restoration, and forgiveness, culminating in the ultimate table of reconciliation—the cross. We invite you to partake in communion and embrace the healing and unity offered through Christ. Don't miss this transformative journey of acceptance, forgiveness, and renewal.

title: But, This I Know
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
Have you ever been put on the spot about something you couldn't fully explain, and felt the pressure of someone expecting more from you than you had to give?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin unpacks a moment in John chapter 9 that is easy to overlook but surprisingly hard to shake. A man who spent his whole life blind gets caught in the middle of a religious controversy he never asked for, and the only thing he can fall back on is the one thing he knows for certain. What starts as a story about a miracle quickly becomes something much more personal, about the difference between knowing facts and knowing someone, and why that distinction matters more than most of us realise. Ps Caleb is honest about uncertainty, refreshingly funny, and gets to something real about what it looks like to keep moving when you do not have all the answers.

Settle in and let this one land.

title: What are you building?
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine you are halfway through building something, a house, a business, a life, and someone asks you what it is actually standing on. Not the walls or the roof or the things people can see from the street, but the foundation underneath all of it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a question that sounds simple on the surface and follows it somewhere unexpected. Starting with one of the most familiar passages in the Bible, he unpacks why hearing the right things is not enough, and why the gap between knowing and doing might be the most important distance any of us ever has to close. Along the way, he brings in an ancient blueprint for a flourishing life that is surprisingly straightforward, and asks some honest questions about what is actually shaping you from the inside out.

Have a listen and find out what your life is standing on.

title: Socially Acceptable
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: "Are we desensitised to 'socially acceptable sins'? Proverbs 6:16-19 reminds us that what society normalises may still grieve God's heart. From gossip to greed, this message challenges us to examine our lives, repent, and align with God's standards. Let's pursue revival through holiness and prayer, keeping our eyes on Christ—the ultimate antidote to sin."

title: Do Not Resist the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us have had a moment where we quietly wondered whether we've been getting this wrong. Not the big stuff, maybe, but the way we hold back. The way we keep things tidy. The way we call it wisdom when it might actually be resistance.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a sharp turn from his planned message because sometimes the most honest thing a preacher can do is follow where he's being led. He unpacks why so many people, including committed churchgoers, quietly push back against the Holy Spirit, through their habits, their theology, their sin, and even their comfort. Along the way, he draws on some surprising moments from Scripture and from his own experience that will make you rethink what you thought you knew about how God moves.

If any of this feels a little close to home, maybe sit with that rather than scroll past it.

title: UGANDA MISSIONS TEAM WRAP
blurb: Hear all of the amazing things we saw and experienced in Uganda

title: Month of Prayer - Revival
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Are we truly hungry for God? Psalm 63:1 reminds us of David's deep thirst for God's presence. Revival begins with conviction, repentance, and prayer. Acts 2 shows the power of unity and hunger for God. What are we willing to sacrifice for revival? Let's make prayer central and seek Him wholeheartedly.

title: Month of Prayer - Radical Devotion
speaker: Ps Keith Ainge
blurb:
Comfort is the quietest enemy of a deeper faith.

In this episode, Ps Keith Ainge brings a grounded and honest conversation about what it really looks like to step outside the ordinary and say yes when it costs you something. He shares from his own life, including a moment on a drive home that quietly redirected everything, and unpacks why following closely after Jesus is less about spiritual heroics and more about a decision anyone can make. There are questions raised here that most people quietly carry but rarely hear addressed out loud, and the answers might surprise you.

Yours to discover.

title: Month of Prayer - Renewal
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
You know that feeling when you've been running on fumes for weeks, going through the motions, saying the right things, but privately wondering if there's anything left in the tank? Ps Rachel Cartledge starts there, in that ordinary, uncomfortable place most of us know but rarely say out loud.

She walks through a surprisingly honest list of signs that we might be running on empty spiritually, and most of us will recognise more than one. She draws on one of the most raw and personal poems in all of ancient literature, written by a man who had everything and still found himself completely hollow inside, to explore what genuine renewal actually looks like and what it costs. It's not a guilt trip, and it's not a pep talk. It's something more honest than either of those things.

Give it a listen and find out what it really takes to start again.

title: Month of Prayer - Repentance
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Everyone wants the blessing, but almost nobody wants what comes before it. That tension sits right at the heart of this episode, and it turns out it's been sitting in plain sight inside a passage most of us thought we already knew.

Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up a familiar section of Joel and finds something that tends to get quietly skipped over. He traces a cycle that runs through some of the most dramatic moments in the Old Testament, a pattern that turns out to look uncomfortably close to where we are right now, in our own lives and in Australian culture. There's a kids' relay race, some stolen chocolate, and a moment where ancient Judah and modern Australia end up closer together than feels comfortable. This isn't a tidy, reassuring conversation about faith. It's an honest look at what we've been avoiding and why it might matter more than we've been willing to admit.

What does it cost to actually want the whole thing, not just the part that feels good?

title: Our Father
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us learned to pray the way we learned to speak in front of a class at school: technically fine, but quietly hoping we're doing it right and that nobody notices how uncertain we feel. That low-grade awkwardness around prayer is more common than you might think, and it usually traces back to a misunderstanding that goes all the way back to the beginning.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge shares a story from his childhood that reframes everything about how we approach God. You'll hear why most people quietly struggle with prayer, what a torn curtain has to do with your everyday life, and how two small words at the start of the most famous prayer ever prayed might completely shift the way you see yourself and God. This one starts somewhere unexpected and ends up somewhere worth going.

What if those two words have always meant more than you realised?

title: The Heart of an Armour Bearer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Are you ready to embrace the heart of an armor bearer? Inspired by 1 Samuel 14, this message challenges us to step out in faith, trust God, and move in unity. Just as Jonathan's armor bearer said, 'I am with you, heart and soul,' we're called to support one another and see God do extraordinary things through us.

title: Armour Bearers
speaker: Ps David McCracken
blurb: Ps David spoke prophetically over the life, direction and future of our church as well as brought insight to many individuals. The overall theme, armour bearers release the victory. This is an important word for Harvest Church

title: How to Talk about Jesus
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb: We're reminded of our calling to share the good news of Jesus with others. This message emphasizes the importance of personal evangelism, rooted in Isaiah 6:8 - 'Here I am. Send me.' We're all called to be evangelists in our daily lives, not just those with a specific gift. The main barriers to sharing our faith often stem from fear - fear of inadequacy, losing reputation, rejection, or appearing hypocritical. To overcome these, we're encouraged to follow Jesus' example of compassion and love for others. The message outlines five key components for effective evangelism: prayer, loving others, sharing the gospel message, telling our personal story, and being obedient despite the results. We're reminded that our job is to sow seeds, while God brings the harvest.

title: Life Lessons from Golf
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this engaging exploration, we're challenged to examine our integrity through the lens of golf and biblical stories. Joseph's unwavering integrity in the face of temptation from Potiphar's wife serves as a powerful example. We're reminded that integrity often comes at a cost, but ultimately leads to greater rewards. The message emphasizes that our true character is revealed when no one is watching, drawing parallels between the hidden moments on a golf course and our daily lives. We're encouraged to 'take the penalty' and do what's right, even when it's difficult, trusting that God sees our hearts and will honor our faithfulness.

title: Great Faith
speaker: Ps Matt Heins
blurb: In this powerful message, we're reminded of the importance of cultivating great faith in our lives. The story of Joseph from Genesis 43 serves as a backdrop to illustrate how we can sometimes get caught up in 'donkey mentalities' - focusing on small, insignificant issues while missing God's bigger picture. We're encouraged to shift our perspective, understanding that God is always moving in our lives, even when we can't see it. The message emphasizes the need to activate our faith through prayer and immersion in God's Word, reminding us that God delights not only in our worship but also in our requests. This teaching challenges us to maintain a healthy disconnect from constant discouragement, drawing inspiration from biblical figures who persevered through trials. As we reflect on these insights, we're inspired to nurture a faith that's ready for the big things God has in store for us.

title: Holy Spirit Fire
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a fire that doesn't consume. It shows up in some of the strangest corners of Scripture, and it has a way of finding people who weren't even looking for it.

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes you through some of the most vivid and unexpected moments in the Bible, from a bizarre ancient covenant ceremony involving split animals, to a shepherd who almost walked straight past the most important conversation of his life. Along the way, he builds a case for something that quietly challenges the way most of us think about what it means to follow Jesus. This isn't a tidy theological lecture. It's honest, a little raw, and at times surprisingly funny.

The thing you've been missing in your faith probably isn't more knowledge, more discipline, or more effort. It might just be a fire you can't manufacture on your own. And it turns out, that fire is closer than you think.

title: The Lord is Near
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: In this powerful exploration of Philippians 4, we're reminded of the transformative power of joy and contentment in our Christian walk. The central message revolves around the profound truth that 'the Lord is near.' This simple yet profound statement serves as the foundation for overcoming anxiety, finding peace, and living a life of rejoicing. We're encouraged to shift our focus from worldly concerns to the presence of God, bringing all our worries to Him in prayer with thanksgiving. This practice unlocks a peace that surpasses all understanding, guarding our hearts and minds in Christ Jesus. The message challenges us to examine how we interpret and apply Scripture, urging us to consider the full context rather than isolated verses. It's a call to root our contentment and joy not in circumstances, but in our relationship with Christ.

title: Tackling The Tensions
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb: In this powerful message, we explore the concept of divine tensions in our faith journey. We're reminded that not all tension is negative - in fact, it's often necessary for growth and strength. Just as a suspension bridge needs tension to function, our spiritual lives often require us to hold seemingly contradictory truths in balance. The Bible itself is full of these 'divine tensions' or paradoxes - like being both a new creation and still being transformed, or experiencing both suffering and glory. Rather than seeing these as contradictions, we're encouraged to approach them with curiosity and humility, like Moses approaching the burning bush. By using our 'spiritual eyes' and stepping closer to investigate, we may find that these tensions are actually holy ground where God reveals Himself to us.

title: Uncomfortable Comfortability
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
...and that's the thing nobody really wants to say out loud. The thing standing between you and the life you actually want probably isn't a lack of faith or effort. It's something you've been holding onto so tightly you've stopped noticing it's even there. And the cost of letting go can feel so heavy that even a genuinely good person could walk away from the best thing they've ever been offered.

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin opens up a familiar Bible story and finds something uncomfortable sitting right at the centre of it. He explores why so many of us can be passionate, sincere, and genuinely hungry for more, and still find ourselves stuck in the same place. You might recognise yourself in the story more than you expect, and the areas where we get stuck might be closer to home than you'd like to admit.

You'll come away with a clearer sense of what comfort is actually costing you, and what it might look like to finally loosen your grip on it.

title: Citizens of Heaven
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: We are not from this world! We have an eternal and heavenly citienship

title: No Turning Back
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself replaying something from the past, not to learn from it, but just because you can't seem to let it go?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge walks through two contrasting stories, one from ancient history and one from the writings of a man who lost everything and called it the best thing that ever happened to him. Along the way, he uses baseball, a DeLorean, and a pillar of salt to explore something that most of us do without even noticing: dragging the past into the future and wondering why we never seem to arrive. This is not a guilt trip and it is not a pep talk. It is something more honest than either of those things.

Settle in and let this one land.

title: Heavenly Wisdom above Earthly Knowledge
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb: Join us as we explore together the book of Philippians with Ps Andrew Cartledge

title: Working Out Salvation
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of faith that looks completely convincing from the outside and barely holds together on the inside, and most of us have lived there longer than we'd like to admit.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most misunderstood tensions in the Christian life: the gap between what we say we believe and how we actually live it out. Drawing from the book of Philippians, he unpacks why unity keeps falling apart, what humility actually costs, and why a donkey illustration might be one of the most honest descriptions of how Christians treat each other you will ever hear. There is also a surprising look at a literary device buried in an ancient letter that changes the way you see the entire story of Jesus.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: Joy in Suffering
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
To live is Christ, and to die is gain. Paul wrote those words from a prison cell, and somehow they read less like despair and more like freedom.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up the Book of Philippians and takes us inside the story of a man writing about joy from exactly that kind of place. Before he gets to the good stuff, he lays some groundwork about how we read the Bible that might just change the way you've been approaching it your whole life. There's history, there's context, and there's a thread running through it all that connects ancient suffering to something deeply relevant right now.

The worst thing that happened to Paul might be the reason you're encouraged today.

Unchained.

title: Travel Light
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Not yours to carry.

That is the quiet realisation at the centre of this episode, and Ps Rachel Cartledge traces it back to a sleepless night, a familiar verse, and a single Greek word from 1 Peter 5 that reframes what handing something over actually looks like. Because most of us do hand things over, at least briefly, and then we quietly take them back before anything can change. She looks at why that happens, and she builds a portrait of the kind of God you are supposedly trusting with your heaviest stuff. It is more specific and more compelling than you might expect.

This one is for anyone who has ever prayed something over and then picked it straight back up again.

title: On Mission
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You are sitting in a small country church in regional Victoria, singing songs and listening to a sermon, and it would be easy to assume the reach of that moment stops at the car park. Ps Andrew Cartledge wants to suggest otherwise.

In this episode, Ps Andrew takes Harvest Church through what it actually means to be a church that looks beyond its own walls. He gets into the uncomfortable questions about why any local church should care about what happens on the other side of the world, and he does not let the audience off the hook easily. You will hear stories that are hard to forget, meet some remarkable people doing extraordinary things in places most of us will never visit, and find yourself rethinking what it means to be part of something bigger than your own backyard. Children in Kolkata, farmers in Georgia, street kids in Lesotho: all of them somehow connected to a congregation in a small Australian country town.

There has never been a better moment to reconsider what your local church is actually for, and this conversation is a good place to start.

title: Pentecost Sunday
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Somewhere in the middle of this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge mentions that Pentecost was not a new idea. It was a Jewish festival long before it became a Christian moment, and that one small detail quietly reframes everything that follows.

From there, he traces a thread from ancient harvests all the way to a room full of people waiting for something they had never seen before, and then brings that same moment into ordinary, everyday life. There is more here than tongues and fire. Ps Andrew unpacks four markers that most Pentecostal churches rarely talk about, and at least one of them will probably catch you off guard.

This is the kind of episode worth coming back to. Not just to catch what you missed the first time, but because the further you get from it, the more it tends to surface in the background of things you thought you already understood.

title: Just One Small Jar Of Oil
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
They say bring what you have. But what if what you have is so small you almost didn't mention it?

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes an ancient story from the book of Second Kings and opens it up in a way that feels surprisingly personal and immediate. She brings her own moments of feeling completely out of her depth, as a mum, as a student, as someone standing in front of a room wondering if she has anything worth giving. What unfolds is a conversation about what happens when we stop pretending we have it together and bring our nothing to the table instead. This is not a tidy, triumphant story. It is honest, warm, and at times unexpectedly funny.

This one might ask you to look a little honestly at whatever small thing you've been quietly dismissing as not enough. If you're not quite ready for that, it can wait. But if you are, it's worth your time.

title: Joy in the Spirit
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
You know that feeling when everything around you is fine on paper, but something still feels off, like you're waiting for a reason to actually feel okay? Or the opposite, when things are genuinely hard and you're watching other people seem completely at peace and you can't figure out how they're doing it?

Ps Caleb McLaughlin takes an honest look at what joy actually is, and what it is not. He gets into the gap between the kind of happiness the world chases and something far more grounded, something that holds up when life gets hard. Through a handful of unexpectedly funny personal stories and some passages from the Bible that hit differently in context, Caleb builds a case for why real joy might be less about feeling good and more about what you know to be true. This one gets personal toward the end, and that is where it gets genuinely interesting.

Worth the listen.

title: Gospel Participants
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people treat faith like a finish line, and that might be exactly where things go wrong.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up Philippians 1 and explores what it really means to be included in something you did not earn, commissioned for something you cannot ignore, and still being shaped into someone you have not yet become. There is a thread running through this passage that connects identity, purpose, and promise in a way that might quietly challenge some assumptions you have carried for a long time. If you have ever wondered whether faith is just a destination or something more like an ongoing renovation, this conversation is worth your time.

You will not hear the word "participation" the same way again.

title: Power of Pentecost
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people already know the basic story, or at least they think they do. And that assumption, that they have already figured this one out, might be exactly what is getting in the way.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the most misunderstood moments in the entire Christian story, the day that changed everything and set in motion something that is still unfolding today. He explores what was actually happening in that upper room, why it mattered then, and what it means for ordinary people living ordinary lives right now. You will hear some ideas that might surprise you, some that might challenge you, and at least one that might make you rethink something you thought you already had figured out.

So what would it mean if you had been missing this all along?

title: Light It Up
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there's a world that feels increasingly dark. On the other, there's a church full of people carrying something that could change that, who aren't quite sure they're supposed to use it.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a familiar phrase from the Sermon on the Mount and unpacks what it actually means to be called the light of the world. Not as a metaphor to feel good about, but as a responsibility that changes how you live every single day. She explores what the moon has to do with your faith, why darkness never stands a chance, and what it looks like when Christians stop treating their role in the world as an optional extra. There's a moment in here involving a nearly empty petrol tank on a dark highway that will stick with you longer than you might expect.

This one's for anyone who's ever wondered whether what they carry actually matters.

title: It Is Well
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there is the thing you have waited for and finally received. On the other, there is the moment it is taken away, and you are left standing in front of other people trying to find something to say.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest look at what happens when life does not deliver what we expected, and how we respond when disappointment cuts deeper than just a bad day. Drawing from an often overlooked story tucked away in the Old Testament, he traces the journey of a woman who faced loss in layers, and whose response to each one is surprising, even unsettling. There is something in this story about the gap between what we confess and what we feel, and how those two things can exist at the same time without one canceling out the other.

This one might ask something of you before it's finished.

title: A Different Spirit
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume the difference between bold faith and crippling fear comes down to personality, or maybe just natural confidence. But Ps Rachel Cartledge makes a compelling case that it runs much deeper than that.

In this episode, she takes us into one of the most gripping moments in the Old Testament, where twelve leaders are sent on the same mission, see the same land, and come back with reports that could not be more different. What set one man apart from the rest is not what you might expect, and the question Ps Rachel builds toward is deeply personal: which kind of spirit do you actually have? This is a sermon that challenges you to look honestly at what you focus on, what you remember, and what you really believe when the odds feel stacked against you.

Caleb saw the same giants everyone else saw. The difference was what he did with that.

title: Passion of the Church
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Genuine passion. Not the kind you talk about, but the kind that actually changes how you live, how you move, and what you're willing to give up.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge walks through one of the most striking moments in the Gospel of Mark, where Jesus is out ahead of the crowd on the road to Jerusalem, and something about the way he is walking stops people in their tracks. What was it that the crowd could sense? And what does that moment have to do with the way you and I are living right now? This sermon pulls together big questions about sacrifice, identity, and what we actually value, weaving in some unexpected moments of humour and honesty that make the hard stuff land in a real way. There is something here for anyone who has ever wondered whether faith is supposed to feel like more than this.

Is it possible you already know the answer, and just haven't wanted to sit with it yet?

title: Passion of the Cross
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Three times. Jesus says the same thing three times, and each time his disciples walk away and do something that proves they weren't listening. That detail alone says something worth sitting with.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the more confronting moments in the gospel of Mark, where Jesus makes a shocking prediction, his disciples completely miss the point, and then get caught red-handed arguing about something that reveals a lot more about human nature than most of us are comfortable admitting. There is a reason Jesus had to repeat himself, and understanding why tells you something important about how we all think and what it actually takes to change. This one moves between ancient roads in Galilee and the very modern pressures of comparison, status, and what we secretly believe makes someone worth something.

Worth the listen.

title: Passion of the Christ
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people think passion is something you feel, something that rises up in you and carries you forward. That assumption is worth questioning.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a word we think we understand and turns it completely inside out. He traces three very different kinds of passion, from the desires that quietly pull us off course, to the widespread numbness that has settled over everyday life, to something far older and more costly than either. What he uncovers in the Gospel of Mark is not what most people expect when they hear the word "passion," and that surprise is exactly the point. If you've ever felt like you're just going through the motions, or wondered why your faith feels like it's running on empty, this one is going to get under your skin.

Settle in and let this one land.

title: Open
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
If you have ever felt like you were saying the right things to the right people and somehow nothing was landing, this episode will put that experience in a new light.

Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the strangest and most unsettling passages in the Bible, a moment where God sends a prophet with a message that seems almost designed to fail. But as Andrew unpacks the thread running from Isaiah through to Jesus and the New Testament, something unexpected emerges about what it actually takes to hear, see, and receive what God is saying. It is not the message that needs to change. It is the condition of the person receiving it. This episode asks some honest questions about what it looks like when our hearts, eyes, and ears are closed without us even realising it.

You will not hear the word "open" the same way again.

title: You Need A Bigger Light
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us assume that when life feels dark or empty, we just need more: more comfort, more distraction, more of whatever has worked before. The problem is, that assumption tends to quietly make things worse.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes one bold statement from Jesus and unpacks why it matters more than most of us realise. She traces it back to an ancient celebration, a temple full of flickering lamps, and a moment that was anything but coincidental. Along the way, she gets surprisingly honest about the things we all quietly try when we think no one is looking, and why none of them quite do the job. This is the kind of conversation that starts in scripture and ends somewhere very close to home.

If you have a few minutes today, sit with this one and ask yourself honestly whether the light you have been settling for is actually enough.

title: You Will Be My Witnesses
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Being sent somewhere you've never been, by someone you don't fully know, to say something you're still working out: that is the tension sitting at the heart of this episode, and Ps Andrew Cartledge doesn't let you skip past it.

Before getting to the "go," he spends time on the "who," unpacking the identity of Jesus and the weight of what he actually accomplished. By the time he lands on Acts 1:8, the familiar words carry a different kind of gravity. This is a sermon about witnesses, but it is really asking whether you know what you are testifying to, and whether that changes how you live from Monday onwards.

Somewhere in the middle of it all, he stops on a single word in that passage. Not "go," not "witness," but "will." Sit with that one.

title: Send Me, I'll Go
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us find it easier to stay busy than to stop and honestly ask whether we are actually available to God, not in theory, but in the way that costs something real.

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at one of the most confronting moments in the entire Bible, where a man comes face to face with something so overwhelming it brings him to his knees. What follows is a sequence that is raw, unexpected, and oddly familiar. There is something in this passage that cuts through the noise of everyday life and asks a question most of us would rather not sit with too long. This is not a comfortable sermon, but it is an honest one, and it builds toward something worth hearing.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: Eyes Wide Open
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Somewhere in Uganda, a man with almost nothing looked Ps Andrew Cartledge in the eye and smiled like someone who had everything. That small moment turned out to be the thread that unravelled something much bigger.

Ps Andrew Cartledge returns from Uganda with something he wasn't expecting, and it has nothing to do with what he saw on a screen or read in a book. In this episode, he shares an honest, unfiltered account of what it felt like to have his assumptions quietly dismantled, one encounter at a time. There are moments here that will make you rethink comfort, comparison, and what it actually means to rely on something bigger than yourself. This is not a guilt trip. It is an invitation to see differently.
