When you're done listening, sit with this one question: what would change if you stopped looking away?

title: Return To Your Shepherd
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
Most people have wandered further than they realise, and most people have no idea how close the way back actually is.

In this episode, Ps Ruth Emmerson takes a look at one of the oldest images in human history and asks what it actually means for your life right now. She walks through what kind of shepherd Jesus really is, and the answer might surprise you, especially if you've always pictured God as someone waiting to correct you rather than come after you. This is a conversation about what it looks like to be truly known, truly led, and truly cared for, in every season, not just the easy ones.

This is the kind of episode worth coming back to when you need the reminder most.

title: Opportunity in the Ordinary
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
They say the Holy Spirit moves like the wind, you can't see where it comes from or where it's going. But what if the harder problem isn't tracking the wind, it's actually stopping long enough to notice it's blowing?

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin takes a close look at a story from the book of Acts that is equal parts ordinary and extraordinary. He explores what it actually takes to notice what God might be doing in the middle of a busy, distracted, everyday life, and why being spiritually ready is only half the equation. There's something in here about a tuna pasta bake, a 3am prayer walk gone wrong, and a conversation that probably changed the course of someone's eternal life, all of which point to the same uncomfortable question: are we actually prepared to respond when the moment arrives?

You can't see where the wind is going. But Philip could. And this episode is about learning to do what he did.

title: Communion - Bread and Blood
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The bread and wine of communion are pointing to something much older and much bigger than a church ritual.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a familiar story and pulls back a layer most people never get to see. From a field in Galilee to a manger in Bethlehem to a cross outside Jerusalem, he traces a thread through scripture that connects bread, blood, and covenant in a way that makes the whole thing feel less like religion and more like a story that was always building toward something. If you have ever sat through a communion service and wondered what you were actually supposed to be feeling, this episode might help you understand why it matters more than you thought.

Maybe the question worth sitting with is not what communion means, but what it means that you keep coming back to the table.

title: The Practice of the Presence
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
Most people assume that if God is in something, it will feel like it. That the right path will come with some sense of peace, or at least the absence of hostility. This episode quietly dismantles that idea.

Ps Caleb McLaughlin shares a story from his own life that is equal parts honest and unexpected. He takes us into a world far from church culture, where his faith was treated less like something to be respected and more like a target. Along the way, he draws a surprising connection to one of the oldest figures in the Bible and what that ancient story might say about the situations we find ourselves in today. This is not a tidy, theoretical talk. It is personal, it is grounded, and it asks something real of the listener.

Something shifted for Ps Caleb when he stopped talking to God about his circumstances and started listening. Follow this one and see where it takes you.

title: Three Wise Women
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
If you've ever felt like your life is running behind schedule, or that the thing you're waiting for has been waiting too long, this episode might be exactly what you need to hear.

Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a fresh look at three women from the Christmas story whose lives were marked by disappointment, uncertainty, and loss. Each one faced circumstances that could have broken them, and each one made a choice that changed everything. What they did in those moments, and why it mattered, might reframe the way you see your own waiting, your own grief, and your own unanswered prayers.

Worth the listen.

title: How Then Shall We Live?
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine sitting down at the end of a regular day, looking back at how you actually lived it, and noticing the gap between the person you meant to be and the person who showed up. Most of us know that feeling well, even if we rarely say it out loud.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into a tension that most of us feel but rarely talk about honestly: the pull between the life we say we want and the habits we keep returning to. Drawing on the story of ancient Israel and some surprisingly raw reflections on his own struggles, Andrew walks through practices that are less about trying harder and more about reorienting everything. There is a moment in this sermon where he asks a question about holiness and what it means for how we represent Christ in ordinary life that might just stop you in your tracks. It is not a comfortable question, but it is a genuinely important one.

This is the kind of episode that tends to come back to you later in the day, and you might find yourself wanting to talk it through with someone.

title: Kingdom-Centric Financial Habits
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us quietly wonder if we're doing enough with what we have, and most of us quietly change the subject before we get a real answer.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge tackles one of the topics people least expect to hear about on a Sunday morning, and does it without apology. He digs into some deeply held assumptions about wealth, generosity, and what it actually means to trust God with your finances. You might find yourself nodding along, or you might find yourself quietly uncomfortable, and either way that's probably a good sign.

If you've ever felt like financial freedom was for other people, or wondered whether faith and money even belong in the same conversation, this one is worth your time.

Is it possible you've been holding your finances a little too tightly, and you've known it all along?

title: Losing Control
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You know the feeling. Something doesn't go your way, or someone makes a call you wouldn't have made, and something in you tightens. You smile, maybe. You comply. But inside, you're holding on for dear life.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets honest about one of the most uncomfortable topics in the Christian life: submission. Not the kind that gets preached at you like a rule, but the kind that Jesus himself practised in the garden when everything in him wanted a different outcome. You'll hear a fresh take on the difference between commitment and submission, and why that distinction might be the thing that changes how you navigate authority, frustration, and the moments when life doesn't go the way you planned. This one will sit with you long after it ends.

Let go.

title: How To Stay Close To God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people already know what helps them stay close to God. The problem isn't knowledge. It's the gap between knowing and actually doing it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets refreshingly honest about that gap, walking through some of the oldest, most tested spiritual practices in the Christian tradition and tackling head-on why so many people quietly give up on them. There's a moment in here where a simple email analogy reframes the whole conversation in a way that might just stick with you for days.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: How To Come Close To God
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Feeling distant from God is not a personality flaw. It might just be a method problem.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church gets honest about why so many people feel spiritually stuck even when they genuinely want more. He draws on some surprising tensions in Scripture, a steak dinner analogy you will not forget, and a simple but confronting question about what you are actually offering God with your time. This is the first in a series exploring practices that have been around for centuries but that most modern believers have quietly abandoned without realising the cost.

If any of that sounds familiar, no pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: The Good Portion
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
"Be careful for nothing," the old verse says. But most of us are careful for everything, especially the things we do in the name of God.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a familiar story and asks an uncomfortable question about where we actually find ourselves in it. She unpacks the tension between doing and being, between serving and sitting, and why so many of us are spiritually running on empty despite giving everything we have. You might be surprised by what she says is the real cause of burnout, and even more surprised by what she says is the cure. This is not a guilt trip about what you are missing. It is more like a conversation about what is already waiting for you.

You will finish this episode with a name for something you have been feeling for a while, and a clearer sense of what it looks like to actually choose the good portion.

title: The Prayer of Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of faith that looks like prayer but doesn't really expect anything. It's the kind most of us practise more than we'd like to admit, the vague, hopeful kind where we're not sure anyone's actually listening, and we're not sure it matters either way.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most specific and practical passages in the Bible about prayer and healing, and what he finds there might challenge some assumptions you didn't even know you had. There's a kind of prayer described in James chapter 5 that is very different from the default version, and Andrew makes a sharp distinction between the two. He also gets into why forgiveness and unconfessed sin might be more connected to physical healing than most people ever consider, and what it actually looks like for a church community to take that seriously together.

If you've ever wondered whether prayer does anything real, this one is worth your time right now.

title: Warnings Against Sin
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Honestly, most of us assume we're doing okay spiritually as long as we're not doing anything obviously wrong. That assumption might be worth questioning.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through a passage in James that has a way of getting under your skin. He unpacks three specific patterns that most people never think of as sin, and at least one of them will probably sound uncomfortably familiar. There's a story from a village in the Philippines that stops the sermon in its tracks, a reference to the final episode of Seinfeld that lands harder than you'd expect, and a question about your own community that might be harder to shake than you'd like.

If you're someone who tends to feel quietly confident about where your life is headed, this one is especially for you.

title: The War Within
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The biggest battle most of us are fighting isn't out there in the world. It's somewhere much closer, and it has a way of spilling into our relationships, our communities, and even our churches before we realise what's happening.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the most honest and confronting passages in the New Testament, and what he finds there might make you uncomfortable in the best possible way. He tackles some questions most of us quietly wrestle with: why do we keep doing the things we hate, why do Christians fight each other, and why do we expect the world to behave like it already knows Jesus? There is a moment in this sermon where he makes a point about judgment and the world that is genuinely surprising, and it has a way of shifting how you see things around you. The answer he lands on is simple, but sitting with it is anything but easy.

Settle in and let this one land.

title: The Right Tools
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Put on the full armour of God. It's one of those instructions that sounds simple until you actually try to live it.

Most of us walk into difficult situations feeling underprepared, whether that's conflict at home, pressure at work, or the quiet sense that something bigger is working against us. But what if the problem isn't your circumstances, it's that you haven't equipped yourself properly for them?

In this Father's Day sermon from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a familiar passage from Ephesians and makes it feel anything but familiar. Expect tool belts, steel cap boots, a fire extinguisher, and one very stubborn belt buckle. Beneath the laughs, though, there's a genuinely honest conversation happening about strength, what it really means, where it actually comes from, and why so many people are walking through life without the things they need most.

You won't hear "put on the full armour" the same way again.

title: The War of Wisdom
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine you're making a decision you feel genuinely good about, confident, even a little proud of your own clear thinking. Now imagine finding out that the very instinct guiding you might be the problem.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks a tension hiding inside a few short verses from the book of James, and the picture it paints is surprisingly confronting. There are two kinds of wisdom on offer, and according to James, one of them is described in terms that might genuinely catch you off guard. This isn't a neat self-help framework. It's an honest look at what drives our decisions, our comparisons, and our ambitions, and what it actually looks like to operate from something better.

This one's for anyone who needs to hear it.

title: What do you Want
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine sitting down with someone who asks you one question and then just waits. Not for the polished answer, not for what sounds good, but for what you actually want. For your life, your family, your community.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes that question somewhere you might not expect. Along the way you will hear about a one-of-a-kind pair of shoes, a stranger showing up at a front door, and a servant who climbs a mountain seven times looking for something that isn't there yet. This is a sermon about vision, about the gap between what we can see and what might actually be possible, and about why so many of us stay stuck somewhere in between.

If you have been sitting with a sense that something more is possible but you can't quite name it, this is probably the right episode for this moment.

title: Taming the Tongue
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The tongue is the one part of you that can build someone up and tear them apart with equal ease, sometimes in the same conversation. That tension sits right at the heart of James chapter 3, and it turns out the Bible has more to say about it than most of us are comfortable admitting.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at one of the most honest and uncomfortable passages in the Bible. He walks through the kind of tongue trouble most of us recognise but rarely talk about openly, from gossip and harsh words to outbursts of anger and the quiet poison of flattery. There are no easy answers here, but there is a surprisingly practical framework for understanding why our words get away from us, and what it actually looks like to bring them under control.

By the end, you will have a clearer picture of what James actually says about the one part of your body that might be running the rest of your life, and a few honest questions worth sitting with.

title: Childlike Faith
speaker: Ps Caleb McLaughlin
blurb:
They say faith can move mountains, but nobody tells you that getting there might mean unlearning almost everything you thought you knew.

In this episode, Ps Caleb McLaughlin brings a refreshingly honest perspective to a passage that is easy to skip past but hard to sit with once you really hear it. He asks what it actually means to have a childlike faith, not in a sentimental way, but in a way that might quietly challenge where you've landed in your own journey. From a shopping bag full of bricks to a very embarrassing skate park incident, Caleb uses some genuinely funny moments to get at something that cuts a lot deeper. This one will make you laugh and then make you think.

If you are someone who has been doing faith for a while and quietly wondering if you have drifted further from it than you realised, this one is for you.

title: Free Flowing Faith
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Faith without somewhere to go stagnates. That's not just a metaphor. It's a warning.

Most of us assume that more input equals more growth. More sermons, more worship, more Bible reading. But there's a hidden problem that doesn't get talked about much, and it might be the very reason so many people feel stuck, flat, or spiritually empty.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a detour through the Dead Sea, the book of James, and one of the most unexpectedly honest metaphors you'll ever hear in a church setting. He lays out six signs that something might be blocking your faith from actually going anywhere, and then gets into what it looks like when faith stops being something you collect and starts being something that moves. It's direct, it's a little uncomfortable, and it just might be the conversation you didn't know you needed.

Find out which side of the equation you're actually on.

Flow.

title: Triumph over Temptation
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
...and that is the thing nobody wants to say out loud: the stuff you keep getting pulled toward is not random. It is already inside you, waiting for the right moment.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets honest about why temptation rarely announces itself as something big, how the world keeps quietly shifting the goalposts on what is and is not acceptable, and what it actually looks like to hold your ground when giving in seems like the easier, smarter, or even more reasonable option. Through two very different biblical stories, he shows what triumph over temptation can cost you, and why it is still worth it.

The pull you feel toward the things you know you should walk away from, it is telling you something. This episode is about what that something actually is.

title: Faith Under Fire
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Faith is supposed to hold you together when life falls apart. But for a lot of people, it's the first thing that goes.

In this opening episode of a brand new series through the Book of James, Ps Andrew Cartledge brings something deeply personal into the room, something raw and unresolved, and uses it to explore what it actually means to hold on when the ground disappears beneath you. This isn't a tidy sermon with easy answers. It's an honest look at why hard things happen to faithful people, and what James has to say about the kind of faith that survives the fire.

If you're someone who has believed, trusted, done everything right, and still watched something fall apart, this one is for you.

title: Tools of the Trade
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
You grab your phone at 10pm because sleep isn't coming, or you sit with a sickness that won't shift after weeks, or you find yourself replaying an accusing thought you can't seem to shake. In those moments, most people don't think to reach for anything they picked up at church. And that gap, the one between Sunday morning and the rest of real life, might be costing more than you realise.

Ps Ruth Emmerson brings a warmth and directness that makes you feel like you're sitting across from someone who genuinely wants you to win at life. She walks through a set of practical tools designed not just for Sunday mornings but for those exact moments described above, the late nights, the long weeks, the voices that get too loud. This isn't a lecture about trying harder. It's more like being handed something you didn't know you were missing.

This one is worth your time.

title: Pentecost
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
One hundred and twenty people are sitting in a room in Jerusalem, waiting. Jesus told them to go, and then told them to stay. So they wait, for ten days, while the city fills up around them with thousands of pilgrims arriving for one of the most important festivals on the Jewish calendar.

Most people assume Pentecost got its name from the day the Holy Spirit showed up. But what if that assumption has been quietly flipping the whole story upside down? And what if the timing of that day wasn't a coincidence at all?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a familiar story and starts pulling on threads that most people walk right past. Why did Jesus tell his followers to go, but then immediately tell them to wait? Why that specific day, out of every day on the calendar? And what does an ancient Jewish harvest festival have to do with the birth of a movement that spread across the known world in a matter of months? There is a strategy buried in this story, and once you see it, the whole thing looks different.

You won't hear Pentecost the same way again.

title: Walk This Way
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There is a single word buried in a two-thousand-year-old letter that Ps Andrew Cartledge spends an entire sermon unpacking, and the fact that most people read straight past it is exactly the problem he wants to fix.

This episode of the Harvest Church sermon series goes deep into a corner of the Bible that tends to get quietly skipped, because the language feels too big and too ancient to land with any weight today. But the question underneath it is one most of us carry around without ever putting words to it: what does it actually cost to be made right with someone you've deeply wronged, and what happens when you can't pay that price yourself?

Ps Andrew takes that one word from a letter written to a church in crisis, a community pulled in every direction by competing voices and cultural pressure, and traces it until the full picture comes into focus. What he builds toward is unexpected, and the courtroom scene he sketches near the end is worth staying for.

By the time it's done, you'll have a name for something you've always sensed was true, and a clearer sense of exactly where you stand.

title: Holy Spirit Boldness
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us already know what we should do. We know the conversation we should have, the risk we should take, the moment we should step forward. And still, somehow, we don't. That gap between knowing and doing is uncomfortable to admit, but it's exactly where this episode begins.

Ps Rachel Cartledge from Harvest Church takes an honest look at why good intentions so rarely translate into actual action, and her answer isn't what you'd expect. She digs into the story of two ordinary fishermen who went from hiding in fear to standing boldly in front of the most powerful people in the room, and the question she asks about what changed for them is one worth sitting with. Along the way she gets refreshingly real about her own moments of hesitation and disappointment, and she reframes what boldness actually looks like in everyday life in ways that might surprise you.

This episode asks you to take a careful look at the distance between what you say you want and how you're actually living. That kind of honesty doesn't cost nothing.

title: Revival Ready
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine you have spent years chasing something in your faith life, pouring energy into it, talking about it, praying for it, and then someone gently suggests you might not have actually known what it was all along.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest and sometimes uncomfortable look at one of the most misunderstood words in Christian culture. He unpacks what revival actually is, what it definitely is not, and why so many people spend years running after a counterfeit version of the real thing. Along the way, he introduces five types of people who each have a very different relationship with revival, and chances are, you will recognise yourself in at least one of them.

Is what you have been chasing the real thing?

title: How to Build Your Life
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Two builders finish their houses and wait for the storm. It arrives the same way for both of them, and that is exactly the point.

Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most familiar stories in the Bible and finds something in it that most people completely miss. He asks a question that sounds simple on the surface but gets uncomfortable fast: when the storms come, and they will come, what is actually holding you up? This is not a gentle pat on the back. It is an honest look at priorities, values, and the gap between what we say matters to us and how we actually spend our time and energy.

Worth the listen.

title: One Thing - Inquire
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You are doing the thing. Reading, listening, taking notes, showing up. And somehow it still feels like something is not quite clicking, like you are holding most of the pieces but the picture will not come together.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge wraps up the "One Thing" series through Psalm 27 verse 4 with a look at what it really means to inquire, to study, to sit at the feet of Jesus. He brings two ideas together that you might not expect to find in the same sermon, and the tension between them is worth sitting with. There are some honest questions here about how we learn, where we learn, and whether we have quietly been leaning on the wrong things to carry weight they were never meant to carry. This one does not let you off the hook easily, but it does not leave you without somewhere to go.

The missing piece.

title: One Thing - Gaze
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
A man stands in a garden, looks at a tree, and in that single moment of looking, everything changes. The gaze comes before the reach. It always does.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a single verse from the Psalms and unpacks something that is surprisingly easy to miss: there is a difference between what your eyes take in and what your heart actually sees. You will hear a story from Genesis that reframes everything you thought you knew about making good decisions, a question that is harder to answer than it first appears, and an honest look at why so many of us are gazing at the wrong things without even realising it. This is not about trying harder or being more spiritual. It is about something much simpler, and much more disorienting, than that.

If you have ever felt like you are taking in more and more but somehow seeing less and less, this one is for you.

title: One Thing - Dwell
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You know that feeling of rushing from one thing to the next, always arriving somewhere but never quite settling? Like you're perpetually in transit, always almost there but never actually home?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes one word and unpacks it in a way that might shift how you think about your everyday life. Drawing on some of the most recognisable stories and passages in the Bible, he explores what it actually looks like to stop striving, stop rushing, and simply remain. There's a question woven through this whole conversation that's worth sitting with: what does the fruit of your life say about where your roots are planted?

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: One Thing - Seek
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Most of us have heard that before. But what does it actually look like to take it seriously?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge talks about seeking, not in a vague spiritual sense, but in a way that is surprisingly honest and grounded. He unpacks the difference between chasing outcomes and chasing the source of those outcomes, and why that distinction changes everything. He gets refreshingly candid about his own insecurities as a pastor, the moments where he has felt least qualified yet seen the most happen, and what that taught him about where real transformation actually comes from. Along the way, he draws on some ancient texts and some very modern questions to build a picture of what it actually looks like to pursue God with that kind of bold, persistent, slightly unreasonable hunger.

This one might leave you wanting to talk it through with someone.

title: One Thing - Ask
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there's the pressure to do more, try harder, and fix yourself from the outside in. On the other, there's the quiet possibility that what you actually need is something much simpler, and much harder to admit you want.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an ancient poem, a queen who risked her life to walk into a king's throne room, and a personal story of unanswered prayer and weaves them into something that might just reframe the way you think about asking for what you need. He doesn't tidy everything up or promise easy answers. What he does do is make a case that most of us aren't asking too much, we're asking too little of the right things. There's a moment in this episode where Andrew gets unexpectedly honest about his own faith being tested, and it's worth staying for.

If any part of you suspects you've been holding back from asking for something you genuinely need, this one might be worth sitting with.

title: One Thing
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there's the pressure to do more, be more, keep up with more. On the other, there's this quiet, persistent sense that most of it isn't actually getting you anywhere that matters.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church takes up a question that feels almost countercultural right now: what does it look like to fix your attention on just one thing in a world that is constantly splitting it in a hundred directions? Drawing from a single verse in the Psalms, he traces a thread that runs through the lives of David, Mary and Martha, and the Apostle Paul, and makes a case that the ancient habits we've quietly abandoned might be exactly what we need most today. This isn't about getting your quiet time routine right. It goes deeper than that.

So what's actually keeping you from the one thing that matters most?

title: Planted
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
There's a tree you've probably walked past a hundred times, the kind that barely moves in a storm while everything around it bends. Psalm 1 is essentially a poem about how that happens, and what it has to do with the choices you make on an ordinary Tuesday.

In this sermon, Ps Rachel Cartledge opens up Psalm 1 in a way that feels less like a Bible study and more like a conversation about the decisions that quietly shape everything. She draws on imagery you can actually see and feel, roots, rivers, storms, and trees that don't move, to explore what it really means to be grounded when life gets hard. Whether you're in a dry season right now or just trying to figure out which direction to head, this one will make you think about the paths you're on and why they matter more than you might realise.

You'll come away with a clearer picture of what it looks like to be planted well, and a fresh way of thinking about where you're drawing your water from.

title: Profitable Christianity Part Two
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there's the version of faith that costs you very little. On the other, there's what it actually looks like to belong to a church community, not just attend one, and the gap between those two things is bigger than most people want to admit.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through nine specific responsibilities that come with being part of a church. None of them are complicated. None of them are dramatic. But together, they paint a clear and honest picture of what genuine belonging asks of you, and it's the kind of straight-talking conversation about church life that rarely gets said out loud.

This one might ask you to sit with something uncomfortable about how you've been showing up to your faith community, or whether you've really been showing up at all.

title: Profitable Christianity Part One
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Honestly, most of us have never really sat down and counted the cost of belonging somewhere. We sign up, we show up, and we quietly hope the benefits outweigh whatever we have to give.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church digs into what he calls "profitable Christianity," and it is not what you might expect from that phrase. He walks through an idea that most people quietly resist: that being part of a community means accepting both the rewards and the weight that come with it. Using a surprisingly relatable comparison that moves from babies to bills, he builds a case that will make you rethink what you have been signing up for, or maybe avoiding altogether.

By the end, you will know exactly which side of the ledger you are on.

title: Practical Christianity
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
The earliest followers of Jesus were known for something, and it wasn't their theology or their attendance. It was something far more practical, and far more personal.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a close look at what actually set those first believers apart. She unpacks three areas where real, everyday generosity shows up in a person's life, and the answer to one of them might catch you off guard. There is also a refreshingly honest take on busyness, and why saying no to some things might actually be the most generous thing you can do.

Most of us feel the gap between what we believe and how we actually spend our time, energy, and resources. This episode is worth sitting with if you want to see what it looks like when faith gets off the page and into your week. Give it a listen and see where it takes you.

title: Purposeful Christianity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume that living with purpose is mostly a matter of trying harder or doing more. Ps Andrew Cartledge would say that's exactly the wrong place to start.

In this episode, Ps Andrew from Harvest Church digs into what it actually looks like to live with purpose rather than just good intentions. He tackles a tension that most people feel but rarely name, the pull between the life you want and the life you're actually living. Along the way, he challenges some assumptions that even long-time churchgoers rarely stop to examine, and he doesn't let himself off the hook either. This one gets honest in ways that are uncomfortable and oddly freeing at the same time.

If you've ever felt like you're working hard but somehow standing in the wrong spot, this episode is for you.

title: Peripheral Christianity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
**What's Actually at the Center of Your Life?**

Most of us would say Jesus is at the center of our lives. But what if the way we actually live tells a different story?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through Ephesians chapter one and asks a question that sounds simple but lands harder the longer you sit with it: is your faith central, or has it quietly drifted to the edges? You will hear a fresh look at what it actually means to be "in Christ," not just in belief but in practice, including an honest conversation about why so many people genuinely love Jesus but keep the church at arm's length. It is the kind of sermon that starts warm and gets uncomfortable in the best possible way.

Hit play and find out where you are really standing.

title: The Church People or Place
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of church that most people have accepted without ever really questioning it. The building, the Sunday routine, the event you show up to and then leave. It feels normal because it's familiar, but Ps Andrew Cartledge thinks it might be costing us something we didn't even know we'd lost.

In this episode, Ps Andrew from Harvest Church works through some of the biggest questions people quietly carry about what church actually is, why it exists, and whether it even matters in the world we live in now. He challenges a comfortable assumption that most people, inside the church and out, have never really stopped to examine. What he lands on might reframe not just how you see church, but how you see yourself.

Is it possible you've been showing up to something and missing the whole point of it?

title: The In Between
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
You are halfway up a trail, your legs are burning, the summit is nowhere in sight, and you have absolutely no idea if you took a wrong turn an hour ago. That feeling, that grinding uncertainty of being somewhere in the middle, is exactly where Ps Rachel Cartledge starts this episode.

She traces the story of the Israelites wandering between Egypt and the Promised Land, one of the most familiar stories in the Bible, and finds in it something surprisingly honest about what it actually feels like to be in a season that makes no sense. If you have ever felt like you are moving in the wrong direction, or standing completely still when everything in you wants to go, this one is going to resonate.

Tune in and find out what it really means to trust the route when you cannot see where it leads.

title: Enter His Presence
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most of us have been showing up to church the wrong way our entire lives.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes an honest and at times uncomfortably familiar look at the habits we bring into a church service without even realising it. He draws on an unexpected source, a book that challenges the way modern Christianity has quietly drifted into something it was never meant to be, and he walks through an ancient structure that might reframe everything you thought you knew about what it means to show up. This is not a gentle nudge. It is a genuine rethink of who church is actually for, and the answer might surprise you.

Worth the listen.

title: Closer
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Not more effort. Just closer.

The distance you feel from God might not be a mystery to solve. It might be a choice you're making without even realising it. In this sermon from Harvest Church, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks one of the most straightforward invitations in the Bible and asks why so many of us keep God at arm's length. Along the way he explores what actually happens to a person when they stop treating faith like a Sunday appointment and start treating it like a relationship worth showing up for every day. There are five things that begin to shift in your life when you move closer, and five habits that make that closeness possible. You might be surprised which ones you're already neglecting.

Maybe the question isn't whether there's more to faith than going through the motions. Maybe it's what you're going to do once you know there is.

title: The Power of Passed On Promises
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
On one side, there are people who finished well, who were still holding on to something bigger than themselves right up until the end. On the other, there are people who showed up, went through the motions, and left nothing behind. What separates them is what this episode is actually about.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a hard look at what it means to live a life that matters, not just in the moment, but across generations. He draws on one of the most famous chapters in the Bible and finds something in it that most people walk straight past. Along the way, he brings in a half-finished monument carved into a South Dakota mountain, a man named Noah who quietly checked out for three hundred years, and a personal story about his own father that gets right to the heart of what this whole thing is really about. This is not a comfortable conversation, but it is an honest one, and it raises a question you will keep thinking about long after you finish listening.

This one is worth your time.

title: Your Words Are Your Weapons
speaker: Ps Ruth Emmerson
blurb:
You said something this morning, maybe to a colleague, maybe to yourself in the mirror, maybe just muttered under your breath in traffic. You probably didn't think twice about it. Ps Ruth Emmerson wants you to think twice about it.

She brings something refreshingly honest to this conversation about the words we speak, the words we receive, and the gap between what we mean to say and what actually lands. She gets personal, she gets practical, and she doesn't let anyone off the hook, including herself. This is the kind of sermon that starts with a tube of toothpaste and ends with you rethinking something you said before you even got out of bed this morning.

This one is worth coming back to. The kind of thing that hits differently the second time around, once you've had a chance to notice just how much your words are doing, for better or worse, on an ordinary Tuesday.

title: The Baptism of the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
They say the Spirit blows where it wills, and you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. Most of us nod at that and move on. Ps Andrew Cartledge thinks we should sit with it a little longer.

In this episode, he works through three moments from the book of Acts where the same Spirit showed up in completely different ways, to completely different people, in a completely different order than anyone expected. He walks through the texts carefully, honestly, and with a lot of warmth, and somewhere in the middle of it all, a picture starts to emerge that quietly dismantles some of the assumptions many of us carry into church without even realising it. Whether you grew up in church or you are just starting to ask questions about what faith actually looks like in real life, there is something in this one that will get under your skin.

This week, pay attention to what was happening when Peter was still mid-sentence. It might be the most important detail in the whole story.

title: The Power of the Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
...and that's exactly the problem. You already know what you're supposed to be doing. You know the kind of person you want to be. The gap between that and where you actually are isn't a mystery, it's a frustration you've probably stopped talking about out loud.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes one verse from the book of Acts and sits with that gap for a while. Using a story about a broken-down car and a missionary who spent two years doing things the hard way, Andrew traces what it looks like when someone finally stops relying on their own devices and connects to something bigger. The transformation of one of history's most unlikely speakers sits at the centre of it all, and it's the kind of story that makes you wonder what you've been working around without realising it.

What would actually be different if the connection were already there, and you just hadn't noticed yet.

title: Promise of the Holy Spirit
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
If you have ever felt like your relationship with the Holy Spirit depends on you getting something right first, this episode is going to land differently than you expect.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a long, honest look at who the Holy Spirit actually is, starting from the very first verses of Genesis and tracing a thread that runs all the way through to Jesus himself. Along the way, he challenges an idea that has settled into the language of church without much scrutiny, and the shift in perspective it opens up is not a small one. If you have ever felt like your experience of God was somehow dependent on you doing the right thing or saying the right words first, you are not alone, and Ps Andrew thinks there is a better way to understand what is actually going on.

The Holy Spirit catching our train, not the other way around, changes everything. Worth the listen.

title: Jesus is Part Three
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The closer you get to God, the more obvious it becomes that you cannot get there on your own. That tension sits at the heart of this episode, and it turns out the answer is stranger and more striking than most people expect.

Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks one of the most misunderstood roles of Jesus, exploring why he is described as a mediator and what that actually means for ordinary people. Drawing on ancient roles of prophets, priests, and kings, Andrew builds a picture of Jesus that is far bigger and more surprising than most people have considered. There is a moment in this sermon where a single word from a 2000 year old text reframes everything, and once you hear it framed this way, it is hard to unsee.

If you have ever felt the gap between yourself and God and wondered what to do with it, this is exactly the right moment to listen.

title: Jesus is Part Two
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume they already have a pretty good handle on who Jesus was. Kind, approachable, the kind of teacher who made things simpler for ordinary people. Ps Andrew Cartledge thinks that picture is missing something significant.

In this episode, he digs into who Jesus actually was when he walked the earth, and some of what he finds might surprise you. This is not the gentle, agreeable figure you might have grown up hearing about. The sermon explores Jesus as a teacher whose message cut against the grain of his culture and raised the bar rather than lowering it, leaving his listeners with more to wrestle with, not less. Along the way there are honest questions about how we read ancient texts, what Jesus was really getting at when he asked "who do you say that I am," and why the impossibility of his teaching might actually be the whole point.

This one is worth coming back to more than once. The first listen opens the question. The second one might be where it starts to settle in.

title: Jesus is
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There is a version of Jesus that most of us have been carrying around for years, assembled quietly from the people who raised us, the experiences that shaped us, and the culture we swim in every day. It feels familiar. It might even feel certain. But at some point, if you are honest, you realise you have never really stopped to work out what you actually think.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church takes a question that Jesus himself asked his closest followers and turns it directly on the listener. It is a question that sounds simple on the surface but gets more uncomfortable the longer you sit with it. You will hear why building your faith on feelings and good experiences alone might be leaving you more exposed than you think, and why the answer Peter gives in Matthew 16 is far more loaded and historically significant than most people ever stop to consider.

If you have never really wrestled with who you say Jesus is, this might be a good moment to start.

title: Battle For the Bible
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You pick up your Bible, set it down again, and quietly wonder if it still means anything in a world that has mostly moved on from it. That question is more common than most Christians want to admit, and Ps Andrew Cartledge is not pretending otherwise.

In this episode, he gets into one of the most pressing issues facing the church right now: how do you hold onto a book that the world, and sometimes even the church itself, keeps writing off as outdated, irrelevant, or simply wrong? You will hear where the real attack on the Bible begins, why it cuts deeper than most people realise, and what actually hangs in the balance when Scripture stops being taken seriously. This is not a theology lecture. It is a straight-talking conversation about something that quietly shapes everything else.

Worth the listen.

title: The Table
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
You sit down for dinner, maybe with your family, maybe alone, maybe scrolling your phone at the same time, and it barely registers as anything significant. Just another meal. But that ordinary moment, it turns out, is closer to the heart of what we were made for than most of us realise.

In this episode, Ps Rachel Cartledge takes a simple, familiar image, the table, and unpacks why it keeps showing up at the centre of some of the most important moments in history, and in our own lives. She traces a pattern hidden across three separate stories in the book of Luke that reveals something surprising about blessing, brokenness, and what it means to be given to others. Along the way she reflects honestly on family, memory, and the kind of connection that does not happen in a course or a program but around a meal with real people. This one will make you think differently about your kitchen, your calendar, and maybe even your backyard shed.

If community has felt harder to find lately, this conversation is exactly what this moment needs.

title: Present in the Presence
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You're sitting in a familiar room, in a familiar seat, going through familiar motions, and somewhere underneath it all is a quiet feeling that you're missing something you can't quite name.

In this sermon, Ps Andrew Cartledge explores what it really means to encounter God rather than just attend church. He works through some unexpected stories, some honest confessions, and some passages of Scripture that reframe what power, peace, and purpose actually look like when you stop going through the motions. There's a question in here that might catch you off guard, and once it lands, it's hard to shake.

If you've ever wondered whether there might be more to all of this than you've been experiencing, this one is worth sitting with quietly and letting it do its work.

title: Clothed in Love
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
If you've ever felt like the word "submit" lands differently depending on which side of the relationship you're on, this episode is worth your time.

Most of us have heard that word and either cringed or cheered. But what if the whole conversation has been starting from the wrong place? Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most misunderstood passages in the Bible, and the closer he looks, the more the familiar surface reading starts to shift. He digs into the original Greek, the cultural context, and what Paul was actually asking of each person in a household, and the answers might surprise you. This isn't a comfortable sermon that leaves everyone feeling validated. It's the kind of honest unpacking that asks something real of everyone in the room, husbands especially.

This is one to save and come back to, because chances are you'll hear something different in it the second time around.

title: Turning Misery into Mission
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
They say suffering produces perseverance, but nobody tells you what to do while you are still in the middle of it. Paul did not write his letter to the Colossians from a comfortable chair. He wrote it from a cell, and somehow that changes everything about how you read it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into a part of that letter most of us quietly skip over because it makes us uncomfortable. There is something unexpectedly honest here about the gap between the version of faith we were sold and the one Paul actually lived. Andrew brings a raw, sometimes self-deprecating look at what it means to be on mission when life is genuinely hard, and he unpacks a word buried in the original Greek that quietly reframes everything about why you are here.

Sit with this one.

title: What Are You Wearing
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine someone who genuinely cares about you, someone who knows you well, pulling you aside and asking a simple question: "What are you wearing?"

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes that surprisingly everyday question and turns it into something that cuts much deeper. Using a passage from the book of Colossians, he unpacks the idea that every person is wearing something spiritually, whether they know it or not. Some of it is fresh, some of it is worn out, and some of it has been sitting unopened in a closet for years. This is a conversation about identity, about what we carry into each day, and about why so many people keep reaching for the same tired clothes when there is a whole wardrobe waiting for them.

Have a listen and find out what you might have been wearing without even realising it.

title: Believers Beware
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Threats from the inside. That is what this episode is about, and they are harder to spot than you might think.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a close look at a two-thousand-year-old letter that reads like it was written for today. He unpacks two specific warnings buried in the book of Colossians, warnings about the kinds of ideas and religious pressure that can quietly pull people away from what actually matters. This is not a comfortable, everything-is-fine kind of message. It asks hard questions about what we believe, where those beliefs come from, and whether we are building on something solid or just going along with whatever sounds good.

Find out what Paul was so worked up about from inside a prison cell, why it still matters now, and whether any of those inside threats are closer to home than you would like to admit.

title: Jesus Over Everything
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There's a version of faith that quietly adds things to Jesus, as if he needs a little help to be enough. Most of us have been there, even if we'd never say it out loud.

In this first episode of a four-week series through the book of Colossians, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into a letter written from a prison cell that somehow manages to feel like a warm embrace. The questions it raises are ones people are still wrestling with today: Is Jesus enough on his own, or do we quietly add things to him to feel more complete? What does it mean that he holds all things together? Andrew brings some surprising history, a Leonardo da Vinci story you might not have heard, and a very honest moment about patience that most people will relate to immediately.

This one's for anyone who needs to hear it.

title: Power & Authority
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Power and authority are not the same thing, and the gap between them might be exactly where a lot of people get stuck.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge unpacks a distinction that sits right at the heart of the Christian life, one that most people never stop to examine. Drawing on two specific Greek words from the New Testament, he builds a case that will make you rethink how you approach prayer, faith, and the way you carry yourself in everyday life. There is a moment involving a powerpoint and a wall socket that is surprisingly hard to shake, and a story about a battleship and a lighthouse that lands exactly where you would not expect it to.

This one is worth your time.

title: Money's Test
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
The way you spend money tells the truth about you, whether you are ready to hear it or not. Most of us know we probably should have a budget, but knowing and doing are very different things, and that gap might be costing you more than you realise.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge wraps up a four-week series on money with a straight-talking look at spending, the comparison trap, and why so many lottery winners end up worse off than before they struck it rich. He walks through six practical keys to spending wisely, drawing on some surprisingly direct wisdom from the Bible that has nothing to do with guilt and everything to do with freedom. Whether you feel anxious around money conversations or you have just never had anyone sit down and explain how all the pieces actually fit together, this one is worth your time.

Give it a listen and see where your thinking lands.

title: Money's Spirit and Surrender
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Ps Andrew Cartledge tells a story about a decision he and his wife made with their money that didn't work out the way he expected, at least not right away. What happened over the following year is the kind of thing that's hard to argue with once you've heard it.

In this episode, he walks through two principles most people never think about when it comes to their finances: seeding and saving. He challenges the idea that generosity is just about money, and takes the concept of sowing and reaping well beyond your bank account, into your workplace, your marriage, and even the way you think. This one will have you looking at your everyday decisions in a completely different way.

That story about the decision that didn't deliver the instant result he was hoping for, it turns out that's exactly the point.

title: Money's Pathway
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume that getting on top of money is mainly a practical problem. Better income, better habits, better budgeting. Ps Andrew Cartledge thinks that framing misses the point almost entirely, and this episode is where he makes that case.

He walks through what the Bible actually says about money, and it might not land the way you expect. He unpacks a concept called stewarding, and the way he frames it pulls the whole conversation away from bank balances and into something much bigger. There are honest questions here worth sitting with, and some old ideas about tithing and financial freedom that get a serious rethink. If you have ever felt like money has more control over your decisions than you would like to admit, this episode has something real to offer.

This is one worth coming back to, because the questions it raises tend to keep surfacing long after the first listen.

title: Money Misunderstandings
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
A crowd presses in around Jesus, someone asks about an inheritance dispute, and he does not answer the question they asked. He tells a story about a man with a barn full of grain who thinks his only problem is storage. It is a strange response until you realise Jesus is not talking about the man's bank account. He is talking about what the man actually believes.

Most of us will spend a third of our lives working to earn money, another third dreaming about having more of it, and the last third spending what we made. So why is it the one topic nobody wants to bring up in church?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge from Harvest Church tackles the awkward silence head on. He walks through five common misunderstandings people hold about money, and some of them might surprise you, especially if you have assumed that financial freedom is something that only happens to other people. This is not a lecture about giving more or spending less. It is an honest look at where our ideas about money actually come from, and whether those ideas are working for us or quietly working against us.

Be warned: this one might ask you to sit with something uncomfortable about the story you have been telling yourself.

title: A Seat At The Table
speaker: Ps Rachel Cartledge
blurb:
That quiet ache of feeling like everyone else got a seat but yours was somehow forgotten.

Ps Rachel Cartledge takes an unexpected detour through an ancient story most people have never heard of, and somehow it lands right in the middle of the everyday moments: dinner tables, lockdowns, broken promises, and the quiet weight of feeling like you are living in the middle of nowhere. There is a character in this episode who loses everything in a single day, ends up forgotten in a place whose name literally means "nothing," and who fully expects the worst when the king comes calling. What happens next is not what anyone in that room saw coming. This episode sits with the tension between what life promised and what it actually delivered, and it does not rush to a tidy answer.

Pull up a chair and have a listen.

title: How To Have A Healthy Life Pt.3
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself doing the exact thing you promised yourself you wouldn't do, and had no real explanation for why?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets into territory that most people don't talk about openly: the part of you that wants to do good but keeps doing the opposite, the slow accumulation of shame and guilt that you barely notice until it's almost too heavy to move, and what it actually means to have a healthy soul. This is not a self-help pep talk. It's an honest, sometimes funny, and surprisingly searching conversation about the invisible war that happens inside every one of us, and where real freedom actually comes from.

Give it a listen and see where it takes you.

title: How To Have A Healthy Life Pt.2
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You know what it feels like. You're tired but you can't sleep. You're trying to do the right things but somehow the basics keep slipping. You're functioning, but not quite thriving, and you can't put your finger on why.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge gets honest about the gap between what we know we should do and what we actually do. He walks through seven practical keys for looking after your body and mind, drawing from some surprising places including a sports performance sleep coach, a moment of accidental marriage comedy, and a few Bible verses that might challenge you more than you expect. This is the kind of conversation that starts with sleep tips and ends somewhere much deeper, so do not bail out before the finish line.

Have a listen and find out what it really means to honour what you've been given.

title: How To Have A Healthy Life
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Ps Andrew Cartledge opens this one with a story about a road trip and a fuel gauge creeping toward empty, and it turns out that moment is about a lot more than petrol.

In this first episode of a brand new series on living a healthy life, Ps Andrew zeros in on the one area that quietly shapes everything else, and it has nothing to do with green smoothies or gym memberships. He breaks down four things that build up inside us without us even noticing, then walks through six practical keys you can actually use. It's honest, grounded, and closer to home than most of us would like to admit.

This is probably one to sit with for a bit after, maybe even pull someone into a conversation about it.

title: Turning Setbacks into Setups
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Most people assume that when things fall apart, it means they were heading in the wrong direction. But what if the collapse itself is part of the path?

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a long, honest look at what happens in the gap between where you are and where you thought you would be. Using the story of a young man who went from being his father's favourite to a prison cell, through no fault of his own, he explores what it actually looks like to keep going when the dream seems dead. There is something quietly surprising in this story, something about the connection between the worst moments of a life and what comes next, that is worth sitting with. This is not a tidy, cheerful answer to hard times. It is something more useful than that.

The question worth sitting with is not whether your setback has a purpose, but whether you would recognise it if it did.

title: Protection & Connection
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Closer than you think. The relationships right in front of you, your marriage, your family, your work life, were actually designed to reflect something much bigger than you. And the way you show up in those relationships is connected to a battle you might not even know you are in.

In this final episode of the All Things New series through the book of Ephesians, Ps Andrew Cartledge tackles some of the most misunderstood passages in the whole Bible. He takes on the topics most people either avoid or get wrong, and reframes them in a way that is surprisingly honest, a little confronting, and genuinely worth sitting with. There is also a second thread running through this conversation that builds quietly in the background, and by the time it lands, you will want to hear it again.

If you have ever felt like your closest relationships are harder than they should be, or that something bigger is going on beneath the surface, this one is for you.

title: Time to Change your Clothes
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Imagine pulling on an old jacket you haven't worn in years and realising it just doesn't fit anymore. Something has changed, and you can't go back to pretending it hasn't.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge digs into one of the most direct passages in the New Testament, and what emerges is less like a spiritual pep talk and more like an honest conversation about the gap between who we say we are and how we actually show up. He works through a series of surprisingly specific instructions about anger, honesty, work, words, and generosity, and the picture that forms is both challenging and genuinely hopeful. If you have ever felt like faith should change something about the way you live but weren't sure exactly what that looks like in practice, this one is worth your time.

This episode is a good place to start.

title: Mature Christianity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Have you ever caught yourself assuming your faith is maturing simply because more time has passed? Most people operate on that assumption without ever questioning it, but the Bible tells a different story.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a long hard look at what the Bible says spiritual maturity actually looks like, and the answer is more practical and more communal than you might expect. He unpacks a substantial stretch of Ephesians that touches on boldness, love without limits, unity without uniformity, and the specific reason the church exists in the first place. There is a moment in this sermon where the description of an immature faith will make you stop and quietly take stock of where you actually are. It is not comfortable, but it is honest.

This one will ask you to sit with some honest questions about yourself, and not everyone will want to do that.

title: Peripheral Christianity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You show up most weeks. You know the songs, you know the people, and you care, in your own way. But somewhere along the line, faith started feeling like something that happens around the edges of your actual life rather than at the centre of it.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge works through one of the most packed chapters in the New Testament and asks a question that is harder to answer than it first appears: what does it actually mean to be a Christian? Not in name, not in habit, but in the way you live, speak, and show up. He unpacks three ideas that have a way of quietly rearranging how you see yourself, your faith, and your place in something much bigger than you.

Give it a listen and see where it takes you.

title: He Tore Down The Walls
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You have probably driven past a neighbourhood you would never think to stop in, or sat in a room and quietly figured out who belonged there and who did not. It happens almost without thinking. We sort, we separate, we move on.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge opens up the book of Ephesians and takes a hard look at why humans have always found ways to divide themselves. He traces something uncomfortable through history, from a half-built tower in ancient Babylon to modern border walls, and lands on an idea that cuts right to the heart of what separates us from each other and from God. You will hear about outsiders and insiders, about a wall that got torn down, and about what it actually means to belong somewhere. This is not a tidy pep talk. It is an honest conversation about the human condition and what changed it.

Give it a listen when you get a chance.

title: Just Blew it
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
You are sitting at your kitchen table, replaying the moment it all went wrong, turning it over and over like you might somehow find a version where you did not mess it up so badly.

In this episode, Ps Andrew Cartledge takes you through some of the most spectacular blowups in history, from a billion dollar Nike disaster to some of the Bible's most famously flawed characters, and what he uncovers along the way might completely reframe how you see your own worst moments. This is not a tidy pep talk or a quick fix. It is an honest look at what happens when things fall apart and what might actually be waiting on the other side. If you have ever sat with the sinking feeling that you have run out of chances, this one is worth your time.

No pressure. Just press play when you're ready.

title: The Foundation
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
A builder stands at the edge of a freshly poured slab, knowing that nothing else can go up until this sets. Nobody admires it. Nobody photographs it. But without it, everything above ground eventually falls.

This sermon sits with one of the most overlooked questions in the Christian life: not what you are building, but what you are building on. Ps Andrew Cartledge works through a claim in 2 Peter that would have sounded scandalous to its original audience, and the implications of that claim reach further than most people expect. There is something here about identity, about the difference between knowing you belong to a family and actually living like you do, and about why the parts of faith that feel the most uncomfortable might be doing the most important work.

Watch this one and let it settle.

title: Goodness
speaker: Ps Greg McKinnon
blurb:
There's a version of goodness that looks fine on the surface but is actually just convenience dressed up as character. It shows up when it's easy, stays quiet when it costs something, and calls itself faith.

This sermon from Ps Greg McKinnon digs into something most of us have never really sat with: the difference between doing good things and actually being good. Drawing from 2 Peter and a handful of stories that will stay with you, Greg unpacks three dimensions of goodness that the English word barely scratches. There's a moment in here involving Queen Esther, a double-booked school tour, and a plane landing in the Hudson River that somehow all point to the same thing. You'll also hear a question about clean hands and a pure heart that is simple enough to brush past and specific enough to stop you cold.

Watch this one when you've got someone nearby you'd want to bring into the conversation after.

He walks through six foundational principles for reading Revelation that most people have never encountered, and then he lands on something in the original Greek of chapter one that quietly shifts everything. The vision of Jesus in Revelation 1 is not what most people expect, and once you see it, it is hard to unsee.

Worth the listen.

title: The Faithful

...and then Jesus looks at a church that's doing everything right, doctrinally sound, working hard, enduring real suffering, and still finds something missing at the very centre of it.

That tension is what sits at the heart of this sermon from Ps Andrew Cartledge, and it doesn't stay comfortable for long. Drawing from the letters to the seven churches in Revelation, this message moves through some uncomfortable territory, asking honest questions about what it actually looks like to follow Jesus when the culture is pushing back hard. There's a moment in here that shifts the whole conversation, where the idea of "conquering" gets completely reframed, and it's not what most people expect. If you've ever felt the slow drift of going through the motions, or the quiet pressure to just blend in, this one is worth your full attention.

Watch to find out what it means to keep your Nikes firmly planted when the enemy whispers that nobody has to know.

title: The Throneroom of Heaven
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There is a door standing open in heaven. Not a metaphor, not a symbol, just a door, open, with a voice on the other side saying come up and see.

This sermon takes you into one of the most layered and vivid scenes in all of Scripture, and Pastor Andrew reads it straight through before unpacking what is actually happening inside it. What you find there is not confusion or dread but a throne room that reframes everything, the chaos you are carrying, the week that has beaten you up, the things that feel completely out of control. There is a detail near the end of this passage that most people walk straight past, and when it lands, it connects back to a moment in the Gospels that might stop you cold. This is the kind of passage you think you know until someone shows you what you have been missing.

If the door is open and the invitation is standing, the only question left is whether you will step through it.

title: God's Love vs God's Wrath
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
There are moments when the world feels like it is unraveling at the seams, when the news is relentless, the suffering seems random, and no one has a satisfying answer for why any of it is happening. You carry that tension quietly, wondering if there is any logic to the chaos at all.

Ps Andrew Cartledge steps into one of the most avoided corners of the entire Bible, the seals, trumpets, and bowls of Revelation, and instead of giving you a timeline or a prediction, he gives you something far more unsettling and far more hopeful. You will see a pattern hidden in plain sight, connecting creation itself to what is unfolding right now. The question of how a loving God could allow so much suffering gets turned completely on its head, and the answer is not what most people expect. This one holds together things that are usually kept apart, and it does not let you stay comfortable in the middle.

You will never hear God's love and God's wrath described as opposites again.
